/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractActivit.title: AbstractActivityParameter
/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractActivit.description:
General parameter value used in one instance of activity.
[Without inheritance, combined specializations.]

Title.title: Title
Title.description: Name of the parameter, used to identify it in the activity. It must have an equivalent in the ActivityTemplate parameters.

Index.title: Index
Index.description: When parameter is an array, used to indicate the index in the array.

Selection.title: Selection
Selection.description: Textual description about how this parameter was selected.

Keys.title: Keys
Keys.description: A nested array describing keys used to identify a parameter value. When multiple values are provided for a given parameter, the key provides a way to identify the parameter through its association with an object, a time index or a parameter array member via ParameterKey value.

items.title: Parameter Key
items.description:
Abstract class describing a key used to identify a parameter value. When multiple values are provided for a given parameter, provides a way to identify the parameter through its association with an object, a time index, an integer... 
[Without inheritance, combined specializations.] Note: floating point numbers are not supported as key values; the numbers have to be formatted as strings for robust equality operations, which are necessary for keys.

ObjectParameterKey.title: Object Parameter Key
ObjectParameterKey.description: Relationship to an object ID, which acts as the parameter.

TimeIndexParameterKey.title: Time Index Parameter Key
TimeIndexParameterKey.description: The time index acting as parameter key value.

ParameterKey.title: Internal Parameter Key
ParameterKey.description: The key name, which establishes an association between parameters.

IntegerParameterKey.title: Integer Parameter Key
IntegerParameterKey.description: Integer value from "ParameterKey" parameter, associated with this parameter. Example: {"ParameterKey": "index", "StringParameterKey: 2}.

StringParameterKey.title: String Parameter Key
StringParameterKey.description: String value from "ParameterKey" parameter, associated with this parameter. Can be used to associate with parameter values of type string or data quantity. In the later case, the string representation of the quantity value will be used. Example: {"ParameterKey": "facies", "StringParameterKey: "shale"}, {"ParameterKey":"depth", "StringParameterKey":"1545.43m"}.

DataObjectParameter.title: Data Object Parameter
DataObjectParameter.description: Parameter referencing to a top level object.

TimeIndexParameter.title: Time Index Parameter
TimeIndexParameter.description: Parameter containing a time index value.  It is assumed that all TimeIndexParameters within an Activity have the same date-time format, which is then described by the FrameOfReference mechanism.

ParameterRoleID.title: Parameter Role
ParameterRoleID.description: Reference data describing how the parameter was used by the activity, such as input, output, control, constraint, agent, predecessor activity, successor activity.

DataQuantityParameterUOMID.title: Data Quantity Parameter UoM ID
DataQuantityParameterUOMID.description: Identifies unit of measure for floating point value.

/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractBinGrid.title: AbstractBinGrid
/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractBinGrid.description: The shared properties for a bin grid.

BinGridName.description: Name of bin grid (e.g., GEOCO_GREENCYN_PHV_2012).  Probably the name as it exists in a separate corporate store if OSDU is not main system.

BinGridTypeID.description: Type of bin grid (Acquisition, Processing, Velocity, MagGrav, Magnetics, Gravity, GeologicModel, Reprojected, etc.)

SourceBinGridID.description: Identifier of the source bin grid as stored in a corporate database/application if OSDU is not main system.

SourceBinGridAppID.description: Identifier (name) of the corporate database/application that stores the source bin grid definitions if OSDU is not main system.

CoveragePercent.description: Nominal design fold as intended by the bin grid definition, expressed as the mode in percentage points (60 fold = 6000%).

BinGridDefinitionMethodTypeID.description: This identifies how the Bin Grid is defined:  4=ABCD four-points method was used to define the grid (P6 parameters are optional and can contain derived values; P6BinNodeIncrementOnIAxis and P6BinNodeIncrementOnJaxis can be used as part of four-point method).  Use a perspective transformation to map between map coordinates and bin coordinates. Note point order.  6=P6 definition method was used to define the bin grid (ABCD points are optional and can contain derived values; ABCDBinGridSpatialLocation must specify the projected CRS).  Use an affine transformation to map between map coordinates and bin coordinates.

ABCDBinGridLocalCoordinates.description: Array of 4 corner points for bin grid in local coordinates: Point A (min inline, min crossline); Point B (min inline, max crossline); Point C (max inline, min crossline); Point D (max inline, max crossline).  If Point D is not given and BinGridDefinitionMethodTypeID=4, it must be supplied, with its spatial location, before ingestion to create a parallelogram in map coordinate space.  Note correspondence of inline=x, crossline=y.

ABCDBinGridSpatialLocation.description: Bin Grid ABCD points containing the projected coordinates, projected CRS and quality metadata.  This attribute is required also for the P6 definition method to define the projected CRS, even if the ABCD coordinates would be optional (recommended to be always calculated).

P6TransformationMethod.description: EPSG code: 9666 for right-handed, 1049 for left-handed.  See IOGP Guidance Note 373-07-2 and 483-6.

P6BinGridOriginI.description: Inline coordinate of tie point (e.g., center or A point)

P6BinGridOriginJ.description: Crossline coordinate of tie point (e.g., center or A point)

P6BinGridOriginEasting.description: Easting coordinate of tie point (e.g., center or A point)

P6BinGridOriginNorthing.description: Northing coordinate of tie point (e.g., center or A point)

P6ScaleFactorOfBinGrid.description: Scale factor for Bin Grid.  If not provided then 1 is assumed. Unit is unity.

P6BinWidthOnIaxis.description: Distance between two inlines at the given increment apart, e.g., 30 m with P6BinNodeIncrementOnIaxis=1.  Unit from projected CRS in ABCDBinGridSpatialLocation

P6BinWidthOnJaxis.description: Distance between two crosslines at the given increment apart, e.g., 25 m with P6BinNodeIncrementOnJaxis=4.  Unit from projected CRS in ABCDBinGridSpatialLocation

P6MapGridBearingOfBinGridJaxis.description: Clockwise angle from grid north (in projCRS) in degrees from 0 to 360 of the direction of increasing crosslines (constant inline), i.e., of the vector from point A to B.

P6BinNodeIncrementOnIaxis.description: Increment (positive integer) for the inline coordinate. If not provided then 1 is assumed.  The bin grid definition is expected to have increment 1 and the increment stored with the SeismicTraceData (“inline increment”) takes precedence over the increment set at the BinGrid.  Alternatively the increments are allowed to be defined with the BinGrid, but this should be avoided to allow for variations in sampling in trace data sets.

P6BinNodeIncrementOnJaxis.description: Increment (positive integer) for the crossline coordinate. If not provided then 1 is assumed.  The bin grid definition is expected to have increment 1 and the increment stored with the SeismicTraceData (“crossline increment”) takes precedence over the increment set at the BinGrid. Alternatively the increments are allowed to be defined with the BinGrid, but this should be avoided to allow for variations in sampling in trace data sets.

Use a perspective transformation to map between map coordinates and bin coordinates. Note point order.  6=P6 definition method was used to define the bin grid (ABCD points are optional and can contain derived values; ABCDBinGridSpatialLocation must specify the projected CRS).  Use an affine transformation to map between map coordinates and bin coordinates.

ABCDBinGridLocalCoordinates.description: DEPRECATED: Use  AbstractGeoJson.PropertiesBinGridCorners properties inside the ABCDBinGridSpatialLocation. Previously:  Array of 4 corner points for bin grid in local coordinates: Point A (min inline, min crossline); Point B (min inline, max crossline); Point C (max inline, min crossline); Point D (max inline, max crossline).  If Point D is not given and BinGridDefinitionMethodTypeID=4, it must be supplied, with its spatial location, before ingestion to create a parallelogram in map coordinate space.  Note correspondence of inline=x, crossline=y.

ABCDBinGridSpatialLocation.description: Bin Grid ABCD points containing the projected coordinates, projected CRS and quality metadata.  This attribute is required also for the P6 definition method to define the projected CRS, even if the ABCD coordinates would be optional (recommended to be always calculated). It is recommended to populate the GeoJSON/AnyCrsGeoJSON with properties according to the AbstractGeoJson.PropertiesBinGridCorners schema fragment.

P6TransformationMethod.description: EPSG code: 9666 for right-handed, 1049 for left-handed.  See IOGP Guidance Note 373-07-2 and 483-6.

P6BinGridOriginI.description: Inline coordinate of tie point (e.g., center or A point)

P6BinGridOriginJ.description: Crossline coordinate of tie point (e.g., center or A point)

P6BinGridOriginEasting.description: Easting coordinate of tie point (e.g., center or A point)

P6BinGridOriginNorthing.description: Northing coordinate of tie point (e.g., center or A point)

P6ScaleFactorOfBinGrid.description: Scale factor for Bin Grid.  If not provided then 1 is assumed. Unit is unity.

P6BinWidthOnIaxis.description: Distance between two inlines at the given increment apart, e.g., 30 m with P6BinNodeIncrementOnIaxis=1.  Unit from projected CRS in ABCDBinGridSpatialLocation

P6BinWidthOnJaxis.description: Distance between two crosslines at the given increment apart, e.g., 25 m with P6BinNodeIncrementOnJaxis=4.  Unit from projected CRS in ABCDBinGridSpatialLocation

P6MapGridBearingOfBinGridJaxis.description: Clockwise angle from grid north (in projCRS) in degrees from 0 to 360 of the direction of increasing crosslines (constant inline), i.e., of the vector from point A to B.

P6BinNodeIncrementOnIaxis.description: Increment (positive integer) for the inline coordinate. If not provided then 1 is assumed.  The bin grid definition is expected to have increment 1 and the increment stored with the SeismicTraceData (“inline increment”) takes precedence over the increment set at the BinGrid.  Alternatively the increments are allowed to be defined with the BinGrid, but this should be avoided to allow for variations in sampling in trace data sets.

P6BinNodeIncrementOnJaxis.description: Increment (positive integer) for the crossline coordinate. If not provided then 1 is assumed.  The bin grid definition is expected to have increment 1 and the increment stored with the SeismicTraceData (“crossline increment”) takes precedence over the increment set at the BinGrid. Alternatively the increments are allowed to be defined with the BinGrid, but this should be avoided to allow for variations in sampling in trace data sets.

It is expected that a VerticalCRSID or a VerticalReferenceID is provided in a given vertical measurement array object, but not both.

/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractLocatio.title: AbstractLocationUncertainty
/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractLocatio.description: A simple uncertainty quantification for a point location.

Radius3D.title: Radius3D
Radius3D.description: Position uncertainty refers to the radius around a given location that is likely to contain the true value of the measurement with a specified confidence level. The position is defined in three-dimensional space with x, y, and z coordinates. For instance, if the location uncertainty radius is 1.5 meters and the confidence level is 1 sigma (approximately 61% using Rayleigh distribution), it means that the actual location is expected to be within a sphere of 1.5 meters radius from the reported position 61% of the time.

ConfidenceLevel.title: ConfidenceLevel
ConfidenceLevel.description: The confidence level, expressed as sigma and using Rayleigh distribution, indicates the degree of certainty that the predicted three-dimensional location is accurate. For example, if the location uncertainty radius is 1.5 meters and the confidence level is 1 sigma, it means that the actual position is expected to fall within a sphere with a radius of 1.5 meters from the reported position 61% of the time. The radius represents the extent of this sphere, defined by the location uncertainty. For a three-dimensional position given in x, y, and z coordinates, the rule of thumb for sigma levels is as follows when using Rayleigh distribution: 1 sigma corresponds to a 61% confidence level, 2 sigma corresponds to a 99% confidence level and 3 sigma corresponds to nearly a 100% confidence level. In comparison, for a one-dimensional case assuming Gaussian distribution, these sigma levels represent: 1 sigma corresponds to a 68% confidence level, 2 sigma corresponds to a 95% confidence level and 3 sigma corresponds to a 99.7% confidence level.

Clarifications: Since Certified is the highest classification of suitable quality, any further change or versioning of a Certified record should be carefully considered and justified. If a Technical Assurance value is not populated then one can assume the data has not been evaluated or its quality is unknown (=Unevaluated). Technical Assurance values are not intended to be used for the identification of a single "preferred" or "definitive" record by comparison with other records.

TechnicalAssurances.title: Technical Assurances
TechnicalAssurances.description: Describes a record's overall suitability for general business consumption in context of one or more workflows/personas based on data quality and reviewer's decisions. Clarifications: Since Certified is the highest classification of suitable quality, any further change or versioning of a Certified record should be carefully considered and justified. If a Technical Assurance value is not populated then one can assume the data has not been evaluated or its quality is unknown (=Unevaluated). Technical Assurance values are not intended to be used for the identification of a single "preferred" or "definitive" record by comparison with other records.

/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractPersist.title: Persistable Reference
/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractPersist.description: So-called persistable reference strings carry a serialized JSON structure simply for convenience of transport; the carrier does not need to understand the internal details. This schema declares the structure of this self-contained reference value payload. PersistableReferences come in various specializations. All variants contain a property "type", which can be used to parse into a specific class. The JSON string-serialized structures are used e.g. in abstract/AbstractMetaItem and in some reference-data entities.

lonMin.description: The left longitude limit in degrees; the longitude can wrap around the datum line - then 'lonMin' is not the minimum longitude. Value range [-180,...,180] degrees from Greenwich.

lonMax.title: Longitude Right
lonMax.description: The right longitude limit in degrees; the longitude can wrap around the datum line - then 'lonMax' is not the maximum longitude. Value range [-180,...,180] degrees from Greenwich.

latMin.title: Latitude Lower
latMin.description: The lower or minimum latitude limit in degrees. Value range from South -90 to 90 North.

latMax.title: Latitude Upper
latMax.description: The upper or maximum latitude limit in degrees. Value range from South -90 to 90 North.

scale.title: Scale Factor

unitABCD.title: Unit Energistics
unitABCD.description: A unit of measure in Energistics ABCD parameterization.

/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractProppan.title: Proppant Agent
/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractProppan.description: Defines the properties of a Proppant and it's test values.

MassAbsorptionCoefficient.title: Mass Absorption Coefficient
MassAbsorptionCoefficient.description: Characterizes how easily radiation passes through a material. This can be used to compute the concentration of proppant in a slurry using a densitometer.

MeshSizeHigh.title: Mesh Size High
MeshSizeHigh.description: Integer high value of sieve mesh size: for 4070 sand, this value is 70. For a 70 sand this would be 70.

MeshSizeLow.title: Mesh Size Low
MeshSizeLow.description: Integer low value of sieve mesh size: for 4070 sand, this value is 40.

UnconfinedCompressiveStrength.title: Unconfined Compressive Strength
UnconfinedCompressiveStrength.description: The unconfined compressive strength of the proppant.

items.title: Stim ISO13503_2 Properties
items.description: ISO13503_2 properties for this proppant agent.

AbsoluteDensity.title: Absolute Density
AbsoluteDensity.description: The density the material would have if no intra-granular porosity is present. (e.g. Boyle's Law porosimetry).

AcidSolubility.title: Acid Solubility
AcidSolubility.description: The solubility of a proppant in 12:3 HCl:HF for 30 minutes at 150°F is an indication of the amount of soluble materials (i.e. carbonates, feldspars, iron oxides, clays, etc) present in the proppant.

ApparentDensity.title: Apparent Density
ApparentDensity.description: Apparent density excludes extra-granular porosity by placing a known mass in a volume of fluid and determining how much of the fluid is displaced (Archimedes).

BulkDensity.title: Bulk Density
BulkDensity.description: Bulk density includes both the proppant and the porosity. This is measured by filling a known volume with dry proppant and measuring the weight.

ClustersPercent.title: Clusters Percent
ClustersPercent.description: Percentage of undesirable agglomerated discrete proppant particles which typically occurs more with inefficiently processed natural sand proppants as opposed to manufactured ceramic proppants. ISO 13503-2 and API RP19C limit the mass of clusters to less than 1%.

items.title: ISO13503_2 Crush Test Data
items.description: ISO13503_2 crush test data for this instance of ISO13503_2 data for the proppant agent.

Fines.title: Fines
Fines.description: Mass percentage of fines after being exposed to stress.

Stress.title: Stress
Stress.description: Stress measured at a point during a crush test.

KValue.title: K Value
KValue.description: Crush test classification indicating the highest stress level at which a proppant generated no more than 10% crushed material rounded down to the nearest 1,000 psi during a crush test. For example, a value of 14 means 14k which is 14000 psi.

LossOnIgnition.title: Loss On Ignition
LossOnIgnition.description: A mass loss (gravimetric) test method applied to coated proppants only, which determines the mass of resin coating applied to a natural sand or manufactured proppant by means of thorough combustion of the flammable resin from the nonflammable proppant. Reported as a % of original mass.

MeanParticleDiameter.title: Mean Particle Diameter
MeanParticleDiameter.description: The mean diameter of particles in a sample of proppant.

MedianParticleDiameter.title: Median Particle Diameter
MedianParticleDiameter.description: The median diameter of particles in a sample of proppant.

Roundness.title: Roundness
Roundness.description: Krumbein Roundness Shape Factor that is a measure of the relative sharpness of grain corners or of grain curvature. Krumbein and Sloss (1963) are the most widely used method of determining shape factors.

items.title: ISO13503_2 Sieve Analysis Data
items.description: ISO13503_2 sieve analysis data for this instance of ISO13503_2 data for the proppant agent.

PercentRetained.title: Percent Retained
PercentRetained.description: The percentage of mass retained in the sieve.

SieveNumber.title: Sieve Number
SieveNumber.description: ASTM US Standard Mesh opening size used in the sieve analysis test. To indicate Pan, use 0.

SpecificGravity.title: Specific Gravity
SpecificGravity.description: Not formally part of ISO 13503.2 properties, the specific gravity is the apparent density of the proppant divided by the density of water.

Sphericity.title: Sphericity
Sphericity.description: Krumbein Sphericity Shape Factor that is a measure of how closely a proppant particle approaches the shape of a sphere. Krumbein and Sloss (1963) are the most widely used method of determining shape factors.

TurbidityNTU.title: Turbidity NTU
TurbidityNTU.description: A measure of water clarity, how much the material suspended in water decreases the passage of light through the water.   Measured according to USEPA 180.1 and expressed in Nephelometric Turbidity Units (NTU).

TurbidityFNU.title: Turbidity FNU
TurbidityFNU.description: A measure of water clarity, how much the material suspended in water decreases the passage of light through the water. Measured according to ISO 7027 and expressed in Formazin Nephelometric Units (FNU).

items.description: ISO13503_5 point properties for this proppant agent.

Temperature.description: The temperature at the time measurements were taken.

SupplierName.description: The name of the proppant supplier.

SupplierID.title: Supplier ID
SupplierID.description: Identifier of service company organisation providing this proppant agent for the stimulation job.

Remarks.title: Remarks
Remarks.description: General remarks about this proppant agent.

QuantitativeAccuracyBandID.description: An approximate quantitative assessment of the quality of a location (accurate to > 500 m (i.e. not very accurate)), to < 1 m, etc.

CoordinateQualityCheckPerformedBy.description: The user who performed the Quality Check.

CoordinateQualityCheckDateTime.description: The date of the Quality Check.

AsIngestedCoordinates.title: As Ingested Coordinates
AsIngestedCoordinates.description: The original or 'as ingested' coordinates (Point, MultiPoint, LineString, MultiLineString, Polygon or MultiPolygon). The name 'AsIngestedCoordinates' was chosen to contrast it to 'OriginalCoordinates', which carries the uncertainty whether any coordinate operations took place before ingestion. In cases where the original CRS is different from the as-ingested CRS, the AppliedOperations can also contain the list of operations applied to the coordinate prior to ingestion. The data structure is similar to GeoJSON FeatureCollection, however in a CRS context explicitly defined within the AbstractAnyCrsFeatureCollection. The coordinate sequence follows GeoJSON standard, i.e. 'eastward/longitude', 'northward/latitude' {, 'upward/height' unless overridden by an explicit direction in the AsIngestedCoordinates.VerticalCoordinateReferenceSystemID}.

Wgs84Coordinates.title: WGS 84 Coordinates
Wgs84Coordinates.description: The normalized coordinates (Point, MultiPoint, LineString, MultiLineString, Polygon or MultiPolygon) based on WGS 84 (EPSG:4326 for 2-dimensional coordinates, EPSG:4326 + EPSG:5714 (MSL) for 3-dimensional coordinates). This derived coordinate representation is intended for global discoverability only. The schema of this substructure is identical to the GeoJSON FeatureCollection https://geojson.org/schema/FeatureCollection.json. The coordinate sequence follows GeoJSON standard, i.e. longitude, latitude {, height}

AppliedOperations.title: Operations Applied
AppliedOperations.description: The audit trail of operations applied to the coordinates from the original state to the current state. The list may contain operations applied prior to ingestion as well as the operations applied to produce the Wgs84Coordinates. The text elements refer to ESRI style CRS and Transformation names, which may have to be translated to EPSG standard names.
example: conversion from ED_1950_UTM_Zone_31N to GCS_European_1950; 1 points converted
transformation GCS_European_1950 to GCS_WGS_1984 using ED_1950_To_WGS_1984_24; 1 points successfully transformed

SpatialParameterTypeID.description: A type of spatial representation of an object, often general (e.g. an Outline, which could be applied to Field, Reservoir, Facility, etc.) or sometimes specific (e.g. Onshore Outline, State Offshore Outline, Federal Offshore Outline, 3 spatial representations that may be used by Countries).

SpatialGeometryTypeID.description: Indicates the expected look of the SpatialParameterType, e.g. Point, MultiPoint, LineString, MultiLineString, Polygon, MultiPolygon. The value constrains the type of geometries in the GeoJSON Wgs84Coordinates and AsIngestedCoordinates.

/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractWellLic.title: AbstractWellLicenseCondition
/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractWellLic.description:
The Well License Condition subset is necessarily abstract, because it is not possible to explicitly capture every kind of condition that may be imposed on a license by an authority, a partner or other stakeholder.  Conditions may be simple or complex, and are usually triggered by date or activity.  They also may specify requirements for how and when they must be completed.  License conditions are increasingly more rigorous,  and data submissions are  considered critical elements by most regulators. Some conditions are one time, and others are repeating.  In general, repeating conditions are tracked as obligations.  

Conditions often have to do with regulatory compliance, environmental stewardship, reporting operations, providing technical or business data, paying fees or obtaining additional approvals under specific circumstances. 

Failure to comply with license conditions can result in fines or other penalties, and license suspension or even revocation.

IsActive.description: A flag indicating whether this condition is currently either active / valid (true) or inactive / invalid (false).

ContactBusinessAssociateID.description: The contact person or organization that provides support for this condition.  Normally this would be someone at the agency who imposed the condition.

DueCondition.description: The state that must be achieved for the condition to become effective. For example, a report may be due 60 days after operations commence (or cease).

DueDate.description: The date that this condition must be fulfilled.

DueFrequency.description: The frequency with which this condition must be met, such as an annual review. Where conditions are cycling in this way, please use the project (for work flow) or obligations ( for payments) module to track completions.

DueTerm.description: The period within which this condition must be satisfied, usually following completion of operations.

EffectiveDate.description: The date on which this row of data first came into effect from a business perspective.

IsExempt.description: A Y/N flag indicating that the holder of the license is exempt from this condition.

ExpiryDate.description: The date on which this condition is no longer in effect for the well license.

FulfilledBy.description: The business associate who fulfilled this condition.

FulfilledDate.description: Fulfilled data is the date that this condition was entirely completed or fulfilled.   This date is assigned from the perspective of the business associate who fulfilled the condition.  Some conditions are ongoing, or repeat over time and are tracked as an obligation.

IsFulfilled.description: A flag indicating that this condition has been fulfilled. This is applicable when a condition is met once.

StratigraphicColumnID.description: A stratigraphic column aggregating StratigraphicColumnInterpretations and eventually StratigraphicUnitInterpretations.

StratigraphicUnitInterpretationID.description: The name of a stratigraphic unit that is named in a license condition.  This could be a formation in which aquifers must be protected, formations into which water or other waste disposal is authorized etc.

StratigraphicRoleTypeID.description: The type of stratigraphy, such as chronostratigraphic, lithostratigraphic, biostratigraphic or sequence stratigraphic.

StratigraphicColumnRankUnitTypeID.description: The optional column rank or level of StratigraphicRoleType (see StratigraphicRoleTypeID) that is identified.

ConditionDescription.description: Narrative descriptive remarks that accompany the license condition. Could include the definition at which the values apply (such as 101.325 kilopascals and 15 degrees Celsius).

ConditionNames.description: Names or code values assigned to a well license condition. Can include any type of condition with the exception of values related to stratigraphic units (explicit), Products (explicit) or values (use numeric values).

ConditionTypeID.description: The type of condition applied to the well license, such as flaring rate, venting rate, production rate, H2S content limit, emissions etc.

ConditionValue.description: The value applied to this condition. For example, an NOX emission limitation may be set at 0.02 kg / hr and the production rate for oil set at 10 m3/day.

SubstanceID.description: When a product or other substance is named as an element in a well license condition, use this reference list to select the product or products.  Production, disposal, analysis, additives and other substances are valid as necessary to describe the condition.

ElementIdentifier.description: Unique identifier of this element in the parent's list of license conditions.

SubstanceLossTypeID.description: The type of loss experienced.  This may include fuel spills from a vehicle, gas emissions from a wellhead or feeder line, or any other substance.  This is an important part of carbon footprint analysis.

SubstanceLossID.description: The identity of any substance that escapes or spills, particularly when unintended. Intended substances and volumes are recorded as production values.

/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractWellLic.title: WellLicenseArea
/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractWellLic.description: Services for a well license may involve field work, office work, legal representation and more.  These services are specific to the license and its management.  Avoid using this subset for other services such as logging, coring, testing, drilling and so on.

ContactBusinessAssociateID.description: The person or organization group who is the primary contact for this service.

Description.description: Narrative remarks about the service provided for the license.

EndTime.description: The time of day on the end date when the service was completed.

RepresentedBusinessAssociateID.description: The business associate on whose behalf the service was provided.

ServiceAgentID.description: The agent through whom a service is brokered or otherwise obtained.  Commonly used where regulations require the use of local agents, or where confidentiality is a concern.

ServiceAgentApprovedDate.description: Service agents work on behalf of a licensee, and must be approved by the regulator. The service agent has legal authority, and the relationship between a regulator, a licensee  is formal.  If the service agent changes, the regulator must be notified and approval for the change given. This is the date that the authority who granted the license gave consent to change the service agent.

ServiceAgentDischargeDate.description: The relationship between a licensee and service agent is formal.  When a service agent is discharged, regulatory notification, and sometimes approval, is required.

ServiceByBusinessAssociateID.description: The business associate who provided the service, generally the supplier.

ServiceForBusinessAssociate.description: The business associate for whom this service was provided, generally the client or customer.

ServiceQualityTypeID.description: This attribute can be used to capture information about the quality of service.  Users of this attribute should be aware that this information may be considered private or privileged, and in some situations data may become public, resulting in violation of certain laws.

ServiceSequenceNumber.description: In some cases, it is necessary to order services in the sequence provided, particularly when there are relationships between the services. Use this number to organize services in the order that they were done in.  Note that some services are not necessarily associated with a date sufficiently accurate to allow this sequencing to be reliably derived.

ServiceTypeID.description: The service provided for the license.  Examples of services may be field related, such as surveys, or back office services such as address for service, accounting, or legal representative.

StartTime.description: The time of start day when the service started.

ElementIdentifier.description: Unique identifier of this element in the parent's list of license services.

/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractWellLic.title: WellLicenseArea
/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractWellLic.description:
A specific well license status value belonging to a well license status class facet, which is assigned by a business
associate and valid for a time interval. It identifies the facility the license status is valid for.

LicenseStatusTypeID.title: License Status Type ID
LicenseStatusTypeID.description: The specific status that is applicable, which belongs to a status class.  They are selected from values organized in a faceted taxonomy, where the status class is the name of a facet. Each status class should represent an element in a faceted taxonomy that reflects one perspective of the state or condition of a data object.

IsActive.title: Is Active
IsActive.description: A flag that indicates whether a particular status is currently in effect.  Historical status information can be retained for legal, administrative or analysis purposes.  Future status information can be projected based on the terms of a license and may also be captured in this data object.

StatusAssignedByID.title: Status Assigned By ID
StatusAssignedByID.description: Identify the business associate who assigned this status.  A status is most commonly assigned by the operator, field contractor, contact for service or the regulatory agency.

StatusEffectiveDate.title: Status Effective Date
StatusEffectiveDate.description: The date on which this status was first valid.  Note that a data object can have more than one status in effect at the same time, provided that there is no conflict or confusion created by doing so.

StatusTerminationDate.title: Status Termination Date
StatusTerminationDate.description: The date on which this status is no longer valid.  A status can become invalid based on events or activities, because they have been superseded by a different status or even because status information is no longer relevant.

WellID.title: Well ID
WellID.description: Identify the well for which this status is valid, particularly useful when a status is applicable for the entire well configuration . Note that these are not well statuses, but license statuses.

WellboreID.title: Wellbore ID
WellboreID.description: Identify the wellbore for which this status is valid, particularly useful when a status is not applicable for the entire well configuration.  In the license, each wellbore may have a different status in terms of the license. Note that these are not well statuses, but license statuses.

StatusReason.title: Status Reason
StatusReason.description: The reason why this status has been assigned to a well license.  This is particularly important if a license has been cancelled, suspended or terminated by a regulatory authority.

ElementIdentifier.title: Element Identifier
ElementIdentifier.description: Unique identifier of this element in the parent's list of license states.

/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractWellLic.title: AbstractWellLicenseViolation
/data/Generated/abstract/AbstractWellLic.description: Violations of license conditions may have serious consequences, including penalties or suspension or revocation of the license.  Any condition may be violated, and the regulator may provide notice to the address for service that the violation must be remedied. These processes are complex, but this simplified subset of attributes allows basic information to be captured.

QuantityLost.description: The liquid or gaseous volume or other quantity that was lost or that escaped.

QuantityLostDuration.description: The duration over which the volume loss was recorded, usually in hours or days.

ViolatedCondition.description: The condition(s) in a license that have been violated.  This may be a relationship to the specific conditions. The ViolatedCondition value refers to an array element in data.LicenseConditions[].

IsActive.description: Indicates whether this violation is still in effect, or has not been fully resolved.

ViolationConsequenceTypeIDs.description: The consequence of the violation as assigned by the regulatory or other authority.  Consequence may be financial, work to be done, reports to be submitted. In addition, the authority may suspend, terminate or otherwise revise a license by adding new conditions or obligations.  For each violation, there may be more than one consequences.

ViolationDate.description: The date on which the violation was first on record, such as the date that the regulatory agency notified you about a problem, or the date when something such as a report was overdue. Violations may be triggered by operations or events (or failure to complete something) or may be reported by another party.

ViolationDescription.description:
A supporting narrative that describes the violation.  While in some cases the nature of the violations, others require detailed explanations.  For example, environmental violations often require explanatory text). 

In populating descriptions of the violation and the resolution, ensure that the contents are appropriate to the attribute.  Do not put resolution information in the violation description, for example.

ViolationEndDate.description: The date on which a violation is determined to have been fully resolved.

ViolationResolutionDescription.description: A short narrative description of the specific resolution of the violation, such as procedures modified, fence repaired, water disposal corrected etc.

ViolationResolutionMethodTypeIDs.description: The method by which a license violation has been resolved.  In some cases, more than one method must be used, so multiple entries may be required, with appropriate dates associated.  Methods may be financial (fines or other payments), operational (procedures altered),  rectification (things fixed or moved) or conciliatory (remedies to citizens or other stakeholders).

ViolationResolvedDate.description: The date that this violation was resolved by submitting required information, paying fines, amending procedures etc. and necessary release notice provided (usually by the regulator).  This may or may not be the same as the ViolationEndDate.

ViolationStartDate.description: The date on which this violation was determined to be in effect.  This may not be the same date as the violation actually first began, ViolationDate.

ViolationTypeID.description: The type of violation of a license that is being recorded. Can be as simple as failure to submit necessary reports or something more difficult such as improper procedures. Grouping these violations by class supports reporting, metrics and analysis.

WellID.description: Identify the well  that is in violation. The condition violated can be tracked via ViolatedCondition referring to an object in data.LicenseConditions[].

WellboreID.description: Identify the wellbore  that is in violation. The condition violated can be tracked via ViolatedCondition referring to an object in data.LicenseConditions[].

ElementIdentifier.description: Unique identifier of this element in the parent's list of license violations.

ColumnBasedTableTemplateID.title: ID of the column based table template used
ColumnBasedTableTemplateID.description: Optional relationship to a ColumnBasedTableTemplate record, which defines the KeyColumn and Column definitions. Some columns defined in the template may be omitted if not contained in the ColumnValues, but the ones used must be exactly identical to the template's column definitions. If the ColumnBasedTableTemplateID is populated, the ColumnBasedTableType is expected to be ColumnBasedTableTemplateControlled.

ColumnBasedTableTypeID.title: Column based Table Type ID
ColumnBasedTableTypeID.description: Quickly indicate the type of the column based table (KrPc, PVT, Facies, ...) and its standard columns definition. It is supposed to be used when you don't use KeyColumns neither Columns as attributes of this WPC.

KeyColumns.title: Key columns
KeyColumns.description: A column whose values are considered as keys/indices. Do not use this attribute if you want to follow a given ColumnBasedTableType.

Columns.title: Common columns
Columns.description: A common column storing values of a particular property kind. Do not use this attribute if you want to follow a given ColumnBasedTableType.

ColumnNamesInFirstRow.title: Column Names In First Row
ColumnNamesInFirstRow.description: If set to true, the first data row contains the ColumnName values or labels for the purpose of checking/constraining the ColumnName in Columns[]/KeyColumns[].

ColumnSpecifications.title: Column Specifications
ColumnSpecifications.description: The column specifications in the order they appear in the data file. ColumnSpecifications[].ColumnName is the key, which matches and links to the Columns[].ColumnName metadata. ColumnSpecifications contain format hints and absent value definitions.

items.title: ColumnSpecification
items.description: Selection criteria to define a subset of a text file row in order to represent the row value in the table column indentified by ColumnName.

ColumnName.title: Column Name
ColumnName.description: The unique name of the column as defined in the column metadata, e.g. dataset--TabularData record. ColumnName is mandatory.

ColumnFormat.title: Column Format
ColumnFormat.description: The fixed format code, I for integer, A for string, F for floating point numbers, followed by a n integer number describing the field length. For floating point numbers (F), the number of decimals is indicated after the decimal point, i.e., F9.2 meaning field length 9 characters including sign and 2 characters behind the decimal point. The value type is defined in the column  metadata.

ColumnByteCount.title: Column Byte Count
ColumnByteCount.description: Only used for fixed format parsing, i.e., when ColumnFormat is populated. It described the length (in bytes) of the column in the table row.

ColumnStartByte.title: Column Start Byte
ColumnStartByte.description: Only used for fixed format parsing, i.e., when ColumnFormat is populated. It defined the start byte (starting with 0) to read the table cell value from.

AbsentValue.title: Absent Value
AbsentValue.description: The value representing an absent value or null value. For fixed format cell values this string value must be compatible with the CellFormat.

ColumnSeparator.title: Column Separator
ColumnSeparator.description: If specified, a cells of a record row are separated by this character, e.g., ',' for comma separated columns. For fixed format record rows the property is left absent or the value as empty string "".

NumberOfRowsToSkip.title: Number of Rows to skip
NumberOfRowsToSkip.description: Sometimes the data file contains header records, which do not contain row data. NumberOfRowsToSkip avoids parsing header rows as data rows. If absent, the default value is 0.

CommentIndicator.title: Comment Indicator
CommentIndicator.description: The start of a comment line, which should be skipped.

EPCFile.title: EPC File
EPCFile.description: Energistics Packaging Conventions (EPC) is a file packaging convention based on the Open Packaging Conventions (OPC), a widely used container-file technology that allows multiple types of files to be bundled together into a single package. Built on the widely used ZIP file structure and originally created by Microsoft, OPC is now an open standard supported by two standards organizations. For more information see energistics (http://docs.energistics.org/#EPC/EPC_TOPICS/EPC-000-000-titlepage.html).

EPCExternalParts.title: EPC External Parts
EPCExternalParts.description: Generally this array contains one HDF5 file when this file collection is used to transfer RESQML2 data. Though, as https://docs.energistics.opengroup.org/EPC/EPC_TOPICS/EPC-000-022-0-C-sv1000.html indicates, EPC external parts are not restricted to HDF5 files only and can be encoded in whatever other format.

EPCFile.title: EPC File
EPCFile.description: Energistics Packaging Conventions (EPC) is a file packaging convention based on the Open Packaging Conventions (OPC), a widely used container-file technology that allows multiple types of files to be bundled together into a single package. Built on the widely used ZIP file structure and originally created by Microsoft, OPC is now an open standard supported by two standards organizations. For more information see energistics (http://docs.energistics.org/#EPC/EPC_TOPICS/EPC-000-000-titlepage.html).

EPCExternalParts.title: EPC External Parts
EPCExternalParts.description: Generally this array contains one HDF5 file when this file collection is used to transfer RESQML2 data. Though, as https://docs.energistics.opengroup.org/EPC/EPC_TOPICS/EPC-000-022-0-C-sv1000.html indicates, EPC external parts are not restricted to HDF5 files only and can be encoded in whatever other format.

/data/Generated/dataset/FileCollection.E.title: FileCollection.Esri.Shape
/data/Generated/dataset/FileCollection.E.description: A dataset representing a shapefile format, i.e. a collection of files with specific extensions. A shapefile is a geospatial vector data format for geographic information system (GIS) software. It is developed and regulated by Esri as a mostly open specification for data interoperability among Esri and other GIS software products. The shapefile format can spatially describe vector features: points, lines, and polygons, representing, for example, water wells, rivers, and lakes. Each item usually has attributes that describe it, such as name or properties. The role of the files in the collection is identified by the standard file extension, e.g. '.dbf', '.shp', '.shx', etc.

SpatialReference.title: Spatial Reference
SpatialReference.description: The geo-spatial reference for the data in the Esri shape file. The definition typically augments the information provided in the .prj file. Augmentation examples: 1) The designated CRS identified by CoordinateReferenceSystemID can be an early BoundCRS providing the selected transformation to WGS 84. 2) If the dataset represents 3-dimensional coordinates, the VerticalCoordinateReferenceSystemID provides the vertical reference. 3) If no vertical CRS is defined, the vertical unit is given by PersistableReferenceUnitZ.

ChunkSize.description: The size of the data chunks (commonly called "brick size") into which the seismic data is divided. Populate one array entry per dimension.

IsLossless.description: A "true" flag indicates that the data compression applied does not lose data (aka lossless), and therefore can be perfectly reconstructed. "False" indicates the compression is "lossy".

CompressionTolerance.description: This tolerance ensures that values (e.g. seismic amplitudes) in the decompressed array differ from the input array by no more than this tolerance. CompressionTolerance is only used when IsLossless = false.

GridOverrides.description: GridOverrides supports processes to re-index and sort seismic data to a logical grid (e.g. 3D Shot Grid or CDP Grid) for SEGY files that lack certain required information in their headers. This is usually used for prestack seismic data.
GridOverrides.title: Grid Overrides

ApplyChannelWrap.description:
Setting this to “true” directs the system to apply a transformation that maps unwrapped (e.g. one cable ends at channel 20, next cable starts at channel 21) sequential channel header "channel" into a wrapped layout (meaning every cable starts at channel 1) when converting from SEGY to MDIO. This process relies on the total number of channels per cable, specified by “ChannelsPerCable.” Because it overrides the default header-parsing logic, it cannot be enabled at the same time as “AutoChannelWrap.”

It is recommended to use ApplyChannelWrap when ingesting 3D Streamer Shots with sequential "channel" numbers in the headers and unknown "cable" number identifiers. Designed to be run in after (and in conjunction with) "CalculateCable".

ChannelsPerCable.description: This attribute specifies the total number of channels (often corresponding to receivers) in each cable used for 3D seismic streamer acquisition. This number is required whenever “ApplyChannelWrap” or "CalculateCable" are "true", as it determines how unwrapped (e.g. one cable ends at channel 20, next cable starts at channel 21) channel numbers are folded into their corresponding cables.

CalculateCable.description:
Setting this to “true” directs the system to compute the cable number identifier using the unwrapped (e.g. one cable ends at 20, next cable starts at 21) channel index and the “ChannelsPerCable.” This calculation helps ensure each channel is assigned to the correct cable.

It is recommended to use this setting when ingesting 3D Streamer Shots with sequential "channel" numbers in the headers and unknown "cable" number identifiers. Designed to be run in prior to (and in conjunction with) "ApplyChannelWrap" when cable numbers are needed.

ApplyAutoChannelWrap.description: Setting this to “true” directs the system to apply a channel-numbering transformation based solely on values found in the seismic headers. Unlike “ApplyChannelWrap,” which requires an explicit “ChannelsPerCable” value, “AutoChannelWrap” uses built-in header data (cable number key "cable" and channel header key "channel"). Cannot be enabled at the same time as “ApplyChannelWrap.”

/data/Generated/manifest/Manifest.1.0.0..title: Load Manifest Schema
/data/Generated/manifest/Manifest.1.0.0..description: Load manifest applicable for all types defined as 'kind', i.e. registered as schemas with the Schema Service. It supports loading of individual 'records' of any group-type or combinations. The load sequence follows a well-defined sequence. The 'ReferenceData' array is processed first (if populated). The 'MasterData' array is processed second (if populated) second. The 'Data' structure is processed last (if populated). Inside the 'Data' property the 'Datasets' array is processed first, followed by the 'WorkProductComponents' array, the 'WorkProduct' is processed last. Any arrays are ordered. should there be interdependencies, the dependent items must be placed behind their relationship targets, e.g. a master-data Well record must placed in the 'MasterData' array before its Wellbores.

ReferenceData.description: Reference-data are submitted as an array of records.

MasterData.description: Master-data are submitted as an array of records.

Data.description: Manifest schema for work-product, work-product-component, dataset ensembles. The items in 'Datasets' are processed first since they are referenced by 'WorkProductComponents' ('data.DatasetIDs[]' and 'data.Artefacts[].ResourceID'). The WorkProduct is processed last collecting the WorkProductComponents.

WorkProduct.description: The work-product component capturing the work-product-component records belonging to this loading/ingestion transaction.

WorkProductComponents.description: The list of work-product-components records. The record ids are internal surrogate keys enabling the association of work-product-component records with the work-product records.

Datasets.description: The list of 'Datasets' or data containers holding the actual data. The record ids are usually internal surrogate keys enabling the association of dataset records with work-product-component records, namely via 'DatasetIDs' and 'Artefacts.ResourceID' (both referring to 'dataset' group-type entity types).

createUser.title: Resource Object Creation User Reference
createUser.description: The user reference, which created the first version of this resource object. Set by the System.

modifyTime.description: Timestamp of the time at which this version of the OSDU resource object was created. Set by the System. The value is a combined date-time string in ISO-8601 given in UTC.

modifyUser.title: Resource Object Version Creation User Reference

ancestry.description: The links to data, which constitute the inputs, from which this record instance is derived.
ancestry.title: Ancestry

meta.description: The Frame of Reference meta data section linking the named properties to self-contained definitions.
meta.title: Frame of Reference Meta Data

WellboreID.title: Wellbore ID
WellboreID.description:
Unique identifier for the wellbore.  This uniquely represents
				the wellbore referenced by the (possibly non-unique) nameWellbore.

Name.title: Name
Name.description: Human recognizable context for the BHA run.

TubularID.title: Tubular ID
TubularID.description: This represents a foreign key to the tubular (assembly) that was utilized in this run.

HoleSectionID.title: Hole Section ID
HoleSectionID.description: This represents a foreign key to the Hole Section in which this BHA Run was performed.

FluidsProgramReference.title: Fluids Program Reference
FluidsProgramReference.description: Used to reference the FluidsProgram object containing a list of fluid intervals for the Wellbore.

FluidsProgramID.title: Fluids Program ID
FluidsProgramID.description: An optional relationship to a FluidsProgram object containing the Fluid Intervals. This is required to support the reference to specific FluidIntervals.

FluidIntervalIdentifiers.title: Fluid Interval Identifiers
FluidIntervalIdentifiers.description: A set of reference to the Fluid intervals  used durning this run. This optional relationship requires that the FluidsProgram object is referenced AND that the FluidsIntervals contained within the FluidsProgram have their FluidIntervalIdentifier populated. (See the FluidsProgram schema for more information on FluidIntervalIdentifiers ).

VerticalMeasurement.title: Vertical Measurement Reference
VerticalMeasurement.description: References an entry in the VerticalMeasurements array for the Wellbore identified by WellboreID, or a standalone vertical reference elevation for all measured depths within the BHA Run record. If this is not populated, the VerticalMeasurement is derived from the Wellbore default Vertical Measure Elevation.

ActivityStartDateTime.title: Activity Start Date-Time
ActivityStartDateTime.description: Date and time that activities started (BHA started to be made up, then Run In Hole)

ActivityStopDateTime.title: Activity Stop Date-Time
ActivityStopDateTime.description: Date and time that activities stopped (BHA was POOH).

DrillingStartDateTime.title: Drilling Start Date-Time
DrillingStartDateTime.description: Start on bottom - date and time.

DrillingStopDateTime.title: Drilling Stop Date-Time
DrillingStopDateTime.description: Start off bottom - date and time.

Dogleg.title: Dogleg
Dogleg.description: Dogleg severity over the depth range of the BHA run.

StatusBhaID.title: Status BHA
StatusBhaID.x-osdu-existing-standard: Proposed reference values: final, progress, plan, unknown

RunParameterPlans.title: Run Parameter Plans
RunParameterPlans.description: Identifiers of the associated run parameter plans.

items.title: Run Parameter Plan
items.description: Operating parameters of a drill string run

RunStartHoleMeasuredDepth.title: Run-Start Hole Measured Depth
RunStartHoleMeasuredDepth.description: The start measured depth of the hole section at the start of the run. Depth relative to Planned wellbore ZDP. Navigate via WellboreID to the side-car WellPlanningWellbore, which holds the depth reference in data.VerticalMeasurement.

RunEndHoleMeasuredDepth.title: Run-End Hole Measured Depth
RunEndHoleMeasuredDepth.description: The end measured depth of the hole section at the end of the run. Depth relative to Planned wellbore ZDP. Navigate via WellboreID to the side-car WellPlanningWellbore, which holds the depth reference in data.VerticalMeasurement.

OperationParameterPlan.title: Operation Parameter Plan
OperationParameterPlan.description: A series of operating parameters observed during the run

RealizationStrategy.title: Realization Strategy
RealizationStrategy.description: The realization strategy utilized in this series of operation parameters

TorqueOnBottomGroup.title: Torque On Bottom Group
TorqueOnBottomGroup.description: A group of parameters that refer to Torque on Bottom

/data/Generated/master-data/Coring.1.0.0.title: Coring
/data/Generated/master-data/Coring.1.0.0.description: The activity of acquiring a core from within a wellbore. The two predominant types are by drilling, or by sidewall. In drilling a cylindrical sample of rock is collected using a core bit in conjunction with a core barrel and core catcher. Sidewall cores are taken from the side of the borehole, usually by a wireline tool. Sidewall cores may be taken using percussion or mechanical drilling.

BottomDepth.title: Bottom Depth

IsOriented.title: Core Oriented Indicator
IsOriented.description: Indicates if the core was oriented.

CoreRemarks.title: Core Remarks
CoreRemarks.description: An array contains narrative remarks pertaining to a core.

RemarkSource.title: Remark Source
RemarkSource.description: The person, vendor, interpreter or other provider of information.

CoreRecoveredDate.title: Core Recovered Date
CoreRecoveredDate.description: The date the core returned to surface.

PreservationTypeID.description: The kind of preservation applied to this conventional coring or sidewall core.

allOf.title: ConventionalOrSidewall

CoreSectionID.description: A unique core section identifier, typically for human consumption.

RecoveredLength.title: Recovered Length
RecoveredLength.description: The length of core section recovered.

TopDepth.title: Top Depth
TopDepth.description: The measured depth at the top of this section, typically in driller's depth.

BottomDepth.title: Bottom Depth
BottomDepth.description: The measured depth at the base of this section, typically driller's depth.

RecoveredLength.title: Recovered Length
RecoveredLength.description: The length of core recovered in this run.

CoreTypeID.title: Core Type ID
CoreTypeID.description: The name identifying the type of coring procedure used to extract the sidewall core, e.g., percussion or rotary (mechanical)  sidewall core.

SidewallCores.title: Sidewall Cores
SidewallCores.description: The array of sidewall core samples, their depth and description.

items.title: SidewallCoreSample
items.description: A core taken during sidewall coring.

SampleID.title: Sample ID
SampleID.description: Typically a sequential number identifying the sidewall core sample.

Depth.title: Depth
Depth.description: The measured depth at position the sidewall core was taken, typically in logger's depth.

Description.title: Description
Description.description: The sidewall core sample description, if available.
Description.example: SANDSTONE:  (100%)  light olive grey, minor light grey to medium light grey, very soft to friable, fine to medium grained, predominantly fine grained, sub-angular, rare sub-rounded, sub-spherical, well to very well sorted, trace weak siliceous cement, trace argillaceous matrix, trace pinkish grey quartz grains, trace micro micas, trace carbonaceous (?) specks, good intergranular visual porosity.

RecoveredLength.title: Recovered Length
RecoveredLength.description: The recovered length of the sidewall core.

PlannedVersusActual.title: Planned versus Actual
PlannedVersusActual.description: The ratio between planned sidewall cores versus the actually retrieved sidewall cores.

/data/Generated/master-data/Coring.1.1.1.title: Coring
/data/Generated/master-data/Coring.1.1.1.description: DEPRECATED: Please use osdu:wks:master-data--Sample:2.1.0 or the latest version instead. Look for the tab sample acquisition. The activity of acquiring a core from within a wellbore. The two predominant types are by drilling, or by sidewall. In drilling a cylindrical sample of rock is collected using a core bit in conjunction with a core barrel and core catcher. Sidewall cores are taken from the side of the borehole, usually by a wireline tool. Sidewall cores may be taken using percussion or mechanical drilling.

ReservoirEvaluations.description: Information regarding the evaluation of the reservoir

HoleSectionID.description: Description of the Hole Section in which the evaluation will be performed

DepthPerforationBase.description: Perforation Base Depth for the DST to run through. Depth relative to Planned wellbore ZDP. Navigate via WellboreID to the side-car WellPlanningWellbore, which holds the depth reference in data.VerticalMeasurement.

items.description: This is a geometric body describing a volume in the earth intended to be a target of one or more wellbores.

Name.title: Name
Name.description: Human recognizable context for the target - the name must be unique within the set.

Type.title: Type
Type.description: The type of the target. Only possible values are: "Geological", "Driller" or "Unknown"

Location.title: Location

Shape.title: Shape
Shape.description: The shape of the target. Examples of this are Elliptical, Point etc
Shape.x-osdu-existing-standard: Proposed reference values: Point, Rectangular, Formation Plane, Circular, Elliptical, Polygon, Other

Dip.title: Dip
Dip.description: Angle of dip of target reference plane with respect to horizontal

DipAzimuth.title: Dip Azimuth
DipAzimuth.description: Direction of dip of target reference plane with respect to north azimuth reference

ThicknessUp.title: Thickness Up
ThicknessUp.description: Height of target top surface above reference plane, measured normal to dip plane

ThicknessDown.title: Thickness Down
ThicknessDown.description: Depth of target bottom surface below reference plane, measured normal to dip plane

Width.title: Width
Width.description: The measured length of a rectangular target along the longest side

Length.title: Length
Length.description: The measured length of a rectangular target along the shortest side

MajorAxis.title: Major Axis
MajorAxis.description: Measured length of the target along Target Ref Azimuth

MinorAxis.title: Minor Axis
MinorAxis.description: Measured length of the target perpendicular to Target Ref Azimuth, assumed to be on target dip, strike, rotation plane.

Radius.title: Radius
Radius.description: Radius of arc for continuous curve segment. Center assumed to be offset from start point normal to its beginning azimuth; positive value is to right, negative to left

GeometrySections.title: Geometry Sections
GeometrySections.description: The geometry sections which define the spatial geometry ot the target

items.title: Geometry Section
items.description: The geometric sections that combine to define the shape of a complex target

LengthRadius.title: Length Radius
LengthRadius.description: Length of straight line section or radius of arc for continuous curve section.

AngleArc.title: AngleArc
AngleArc.description: Direction of straight line section or radius of arc for continuous curve section.

ThicknessAbove.title: Thickness Above
ThicknessAbove.description: Height of target above center point at the start of the section.  In the case of an arc, the thickness above should vary linearly with the arc length.

ThicknessBelow.title: Thickness Below
ThicknessBelow.description: Depth of target below center point at the start of the section. In the case of an arc, the thickness below should vary linearly with the arc length.

Location.title: Location
Location.description: 2D coordinates that defines the start of the section.

SectionTVD.title: Section TVD
SectionTVD.description: True Vertical Depth of this section

Comments.title: Comments
Comments.description: A comment or description of the target

ObjectiveType.title: Objective
ObjectiveType.description: The target could be Primary or Secondary

ParentTargetName.title: Parent Target Name
ParentTargetName.description: Name of the parent target in this set, this one has been defined from (this represents a pointer to the parent target. This may represents a relationship between a driller and geological target).

Name.description: Name of Geometric Target Set

/data/Generated/master-data/GravityMagne.title: GravityMagneticAcquisitionSurvey
/data/Generated/master-data/GravityMagne.description:
A gravity and magnetics acquisition survey is a type of a geophysical survey acquisition and a business project that deploys resources to the field to record (passive) gravity and or magnetic geophysical measurement data.

Several types of gravity and magnetic data can be acquired simultaneously from the same survey, and different acquisition platforms can be used to acquire the data, for example, land, air, marine, satellite and borehole.

It may be referred to as a field survey, acquisition survey, or field program.

DataAcquisitionTypeIDs.title: Data Acquisition Type IDs
DataAcquisitionTypeIDs.description:
The type of gravity and magnetics geophysical data acquired in this survey, for example, gravity, magnetic, full tensor gradiometry/airborne gravity gradiometry.
This could be one or several acquisition types that were acquired simultaneously in the same survey.

AcquisitionPlatformMethodID.title: Acquisition Platform Method
AcquisitionPlatformMethodID.description: The acquisition platform method for this survey, for example, airborne, marine, land, satellite, borehole, ocean bottom, UAV, etc.

OperatingEnvironmentIDs.title: Operating EnvironmentIDs
OperatingEnvironmentIDs.description: Identifies the environmental settings of the survey acquisition, for example, land, marine or transition zone. A survey can be conducted over one or more environments.

AreaCalculated.title: Area Calculated
AreaCalculated.description: The calculated area covered by the survey. This value is often calculated during the loading of the survey

AreaNominal.title: Area Nominal
AreaNominal.description: The nominal area covered by the survey. This value is usually entered by the end user

AverageStationDistance.title: Average Station Distance
AverageStationDistance.description: The average horizontal, or vertical for wellbore/borehole, distance or spacing between sampling stations in length, or a depth for a wellbore/borehole. This value can be calculated for moving platform survey from the time based sampling intervals.

EquipmentDetails.title: Equipment Details
EquipmentDetails.description: An array that describes the equipment sensors, meters or tools used to acquire the geophysical data. One or more items of equipment may be used in a survey acquisition.

items.title: Equipment
items.description: The sensor, meter or tool equipment used to acquire the gravity and magnetic geophysical measurements

Name.title: Name
Name.description:
A name given to a sensor, meter or tool used to acquire gravity or magnetics geophysical data. This could be a common or colloquial name. 
Where possible, for better search results, the manufacturer, model and serial number should be completed also.

Manufacturer.title: Manufacturer
Manufacturer.description: The manufacturer of a sensor, meter or tool used to acquire gravity or magnetics geophysical data.

Model.title: Model
Model.description: The model name or number, typically given by the manufacturer of a sensor, meter or tool used to acquire gravity or magnetics geophysical data.

SerialNumber.title: SerialNumber
SerialNumber.description: The serial number, typically given by the manufacturer, of a sensor, meter or tool used to acquire gravity or magnetics geophysical data.

Remarks.title: Remarks
Remarks.description: An array of remarks about the equipment used to acquire the measurements, for example, the orientation of equipment. This utilises the AbstractRemark fragment.

AcquisitionDateRange.title: Acquisition Date Range
AcquisitionDateRange.description: Describes the start and end date range of the survey acquisition

StartDate.title: StartDate
StartDate.description: The start date of the acquisition survey

EndDate.title: EndDate
EndDate.description: The end date of the acquisition survey

ServiceCompanyID.title: Service CompanyID
ServiceCompanyID.description: The company or organisation that acquired the survey

Remarks.title: Remarks
Remarks.description: General remarks regarding the survey acquisition. An array utilising the AbstractRemark fragment

VerticalMeasurement.title: Vertical Measurement
VerticalMeasurement.description: The vertical measurement reference for a wellbore or borehole acquisition platform, defining the vertical reference datum, elevation and relevant depths.

MovingPlatform.title: Moving Platform
MovingPlatform.description: An array that describes the survey acquisition properties relevant to a moving platform survey, for example, airborne, marine vessel or other moving vehicle

IsMovingPlatformSurvey.title: Is Moving Platform Survey Flag
IsMovingPlatformSurvey.description:
A boolean flag indicating if the survey was acquired from a moving platform, for example, airborne, marine vessel or other moving vehicle. 
This boolean flag also permits a moving platform survey to be identified prior to the loading of the moving platform related properties. 
This should be true if any of the below moving platform properties could be populated now or in the future.

SamplingIntervalTime.title: Sampling Interval Time
SamplingIntervalTime.description: The sampling station intervals recorded in time. Sampling intervals are often received in 1 second intervals or similar and/or p190 for marine data

CalculatedLineLength.title: Calculated Line Length
CalculatedLineLength.description: The total length of the line distance calculated from the line data.

NominalLineLength.title: Nominal Line Length
NominalLineLength.description: The nominal line length covered by the survey. This value is usually entered by the end user. Equivalent to the two boxes for an area.

PrimaryLineSpacing.title: Primary Line Spacing
PrimaryLineSpacing.description: The distance between primary lines. If acquired with seismic data this will be the inline.

TieLineSpacing.title: Tie Line Spacing
TieLineSpacing.description: The distance between lines that intersect the primary lines. These lines are at a different azimuth to the primary lines. Typically perpendicular to the primary line.

FlyingHeightParameters.title: FlyingHeightParameters
FlyingHeightParameters.description: Captures the average flying height and the flying height parameters such as the instrumentation, datum and the clearance method.

ClearanceMethodID.title: Clearance Method ID
ClearanceMethodID.description: The airborne survey ground clearance method, for example, constant or drape.

MeasurementInstrumentationIDs.title: Measurement Instrumentation IDs
MeasurementInstrumentationIDs.description: The instruments or equipment used to measure the specified flying height. See AverageFlyingHeight. This can be one or several different types of equipment, for example, laser scanner, GPS, radar altimeter.

VerticalCoordinateReferenceSystemID.title: Vertical Coordinate Reference System ID
VerticalCoordinateReferenceSystemID.description: The relationship to the vertical CRS defining the absolute reference surface. If both the vertical and horizontal CRS are the same, then the vertical CRS should instead be captured only in the AbstractSpatialLocation.

ExternalTopographicalInformation.title: External Topographical Information
ExternalTopographicalInformation.description: The topographic information utilised in this survey, for example, Shuttle Radar Topography Mission (SRTM) v3.

AverageFlyingHeight.title: Average Flying Height
AverageFlyingHeight.description: The average flying height for this airborne platform survey.

SeismicAcquisitionSurveyID.title: Seismic Acquisition Survey ID
SeismicAcquisitionSurveyID.description:
An association to a seismic acquisition survey when seismic and gravity and magnetic data are acquired simultaneously, typically in the marine environment.
The seismic acquisition survey object contains data relevant to the acquisition such as the survey geometry.

PlatformName.title: Platform Name
PlatformName.description: The free text name of the platform or the vessel that acquired the survey

PrecedingTimeLapseSurveyID.title: Preceding Time Lapse Survey ID
PrecedingTimeLapseSurveyID.description: If populated, this survey is part of a time-lapse survey sequence. It identifies the preceding Gravity Magnetic Acquisition Survey. The first survey in the sequence has an empty or absent PrecedingTimeLapseSurveyID.

/data/Generated/master-data/PerforationJ.title: PerforationJob
/data/Generated/master-data/PerforationJ.description: A Perforation Job describes an activity performed on a well for the purpose of firing perforation guns or puncher inside Casing, Liner or Tubing to create a flow path between the reservoir outside the pipe and the production annulus within the pipe. A Squeeze job is a remedial effort performed to create a temporary flow path to allow cement to be pumped outside the casing to repair the annular seal. Perf Intervals result in the creation of equivalent Wellbore Openings where they are managed as part of the Completion. A Squeeze job would not result in creation of Wellbore Openings as these are temporary to better seal that interval.

/data/Generated/master-data/PerforationJ.title: PerforationJob
/data/Generated/master-data/PerforationJ.description: A Perforation Job describes an activity performed on a well for the purpose of firing perforation guns or puncher inside Casing, Liner or Tubing to create a flow path between the reservoir outside the pipe and the production annulus within the pipe. A Squeeze job is a remedial effort performed to create a temporary flow path to allow cement to be pumped outside the casing to repair the annular seal. Perf Intervals result in the creation of equivalent Wellbore Openings where they are managed as part of the Completion. A Squeeze job would not result in creation of Wellbore Openings as these are temporary to better seal that interval.

A comprehensive set of Segments can be built with a PersistedCollection.

A comprehensive set of Segments can be built with a PersistedCollection.

RigSpecificationsID.title: Rig Specifications ID
RigSpecificationsID.description: Identifies the Rig Specification this Inventory applies to.

RequiredFlowRate.title: Required Flow Rate
RequiredFlowRate.description: Required mud flow rates delivered by the pump system.

SlowCirculationRateDescription.title: Slow Circulation Rates Description
SlowCirculationRateDescription.description:
Description of slow circulation rates (SCR) system.
SCR is the rate at which drilling fluid (mud) is pumped through the wellbore and back to the surface at a deliberately reduced speed.

PowerType.title: Power Type
PowerType.description: The primary energy source used to drive the rig circulation and pressure control equipment (e.g., electric, diesel, diesel‑electric, hydraulic).

BOPPressureRating.title: BOP Pressure Rating
BOPPressureRating.description: The maximum working pressure that the Blowout Preventer (BOP) stack is designed, tested, and certified to safely withstand.

BOPVolume.title: BOP Volume
BOPVolume.description: The total internal fluid capacity of the Blowout Preventer stack, including cavities and flow paths that can contain circulating fluids.

RiserVolume.title: Riser Volume
RiserVolume.description: The total internal fluid capacity of the marine riser or surface riser section between the Blowout Preventer and the rig.

KillLineVolume.title: Kill Line Volume
KillLineVolume.description: The total internal fluid capacity of the fixed kill line between the surface system and the Blowout Preventer kill inlet.

ChokeLineVolume.title: Choke Line Volume
ChokeLineVolume.description: The total internal fluid capacity of the fixed choke line between the Blowout Preventer choke outlet and the choke manifold.

BoostLineVolume.title: Boost Line Volume
BoostLineVolume.description: The total internal fluid capacity of the fixed boost line used to supply additional flow (commonly subsea) to support drilling or circulation operations.

KillLineHoseVolume.title: Kill Line Hose Volume
KillLineHoseVolume.description: The internal fluid capacity of flexible hoses installed in the kill line system.

ChokeLineHoseVolume.title: Choke Line Hose Volume
ChokeLineHoseVolume.description: The internal fluid capacity of flexible hoses installed in the choke line system.

BoosterLineHoseVolume.title: Booster Line Hose Volume
BoosterLineHoseVolume.description: The internal fluid capacity of flexible hoses installed in the booster or boost line system.

CementUnitCementManifoldVolume.title: Cement Unit To Cement Manifold Volume
CementUnitCementManifoldVolume.description: The internal fluid capacity of the flow path between the cement unit discharge and the cement manifold.

CementUnitChokeManifoldVolume.title: Cement Unit To Choke Manifold Volume
CementUnitChokeManifoldVolume.description: The internal fluid capacity of the flow path between the cement unit discharge and the choke manifold.

CementUnitStandpipeManifoldVolume.title: Cement Unit To Standpipe Manifold Volume
CementUnitStandpipeManifoldVolume.description: The internal fluid capacity of the flow path between the cement unit discharge and the standpipe manifold.

MudStandpipeChokeManifoldVolume.title: Mud Standpipe To Choke Manifold Volume
MudStandpipeChokeManifoldVolume.description: The internal fluid capacity of the flow path between the mud standpipe system and the choke manifold.

StandpipeManifoldTopDriveVolume.title: Standpipe Manifold To TopDrive Volume
StandpipeManifoldTopDriveVolume.description: The internal fluid capacity of the flow path between the standpipe manifold and the top drive inlet.

MudPumpsStandpipeManifoldVolume.title: Mud Pumps To Standpipe Manifold Volume
MudPumpsStandpipeManifoldVolume.description: The internal fluid capacity of the flow path between the mud pump discharge and the standpipe manifold.

ChokeManifoldBOPKillVolume.title: Choke Manifold To Blow Out Preventer Kill Volume
ChokeManifoldBOPKillVolume.description: The internal fluid capacity of the flow path between the choke manifold and the BOP kill inlet.

ChokeManifoldBOPChokeVolume.title: Choke Manifold To BlowOut Preventer Choke Volume
ChokeManifoldBOPChokeVolume.description: The internal fluid capacity of the flow path between the choke manifold and the BOP choke outlet or connection.

MudPumpsBOPBoostVolume.title: Mud Pumps To BlowOut Preventer Boost Volume
MudPumpsBOPBoostVolume.description: The internal fluid capacity of the flow path between the mud pump discharge and the BOP boost line inlet.

WellTestStandpipeGooseneckVolume.title: Well Test Standpipe To Gooseneck Volume
WellTestStandpipeGooseneckVolume.description: The internal fluid capacity of the flow path between the well test standpipe and the gooseneck connection used during well testing operations.

Tensioners maintain constant tension on the marine riser or drilling equipment, compensating the vertical motion caused by waves and ocean currents

Suggested types: open flame flare, enclosed flare, smokeless flare
