CurveLithologyID.description: ID of the lithological unit represented by the curve

CurveTransformModelTypeID.description: ID of the empirical calibrated model used for pressure calculations from a petrophysical curve (sonic or resistivity logs), for example 'Eaton' and  'Bowers',...

CurveUOM.description: Unit of Measure of the Physical Quantity Measured by the curve. An ID to relevant unit of measure reference

PressureAtDatum.title: Pressure At Datum
PressureAtDatum.description: Hydrostatic Pressure at the Pressure Datum TVD

PressureDatumTVD.title: Pressure Datum TVD
PressureDatumTVD.description: True Vertical Depth from the Vertical CRS to the datum used for pressure. This is further qualified by associated VerticalCRS property. If no VerticalCRS is populated, assume MSL, and therefore "TVD Subsea". The Vertical CRS of the Datum must be consistent with one defined for the reservoir simulation model.

VerticalCRSID.title: Vertical Coordinate Reference System ID
VerticalCRSID.description: The Vertical Coordinate Reference System defining the origin (i.e., zero point) for the vertical measurements on this data record (e.g. PressureDatum and TopDepth). The most common Vertical CRS in this context is Mean Sea Level. Populating this attribute is especially important when the Vertical CRS is not Mean Sea Level but rather a local alternative like Caspian height or a custom Vertical CRS.

VerticalDatumOffsetToMeanSeaLevel.title: Vertical Datum Offset To Mean Sea Level
VerticalDatumOffsetToMeanSeaLevel.description: If the the vertical measurements on this data record (e.g. PressureDatum and TopDepth) were not referenced from Mean Sea Level, this attribute can capture the difference between the selected Vertical CRS and Mean Sea Level.

FluidContacts.title: Fluid Contacts
FluidContacts.description: List of individual fluid contacts such as gas/oil contact or oil/water contact, with associated parameters.

items.title: Fluid Contact
items.description: Description of an individual fluid contact within a reservoir unit

FluidContactTypeID.title: Fluid Contact Type ID
FluidContactTypeID.description: Identifies the type of a fluid boundary such as oil/water contact.

FluidContactTVD.title: Fluid Contact TVD
FluidContactTVD.description: The true vertical depth from the Vertical CRS to the fluid contact.

CapillaryPressure.title: Capillary Pressure
CapillaryPressure.description: Capillary pressure at the contact defined by the Fluid Contact Type.

ReferenceFluidContactID.title: Reference Fluid Contact ID
ReferenceFluidContactID.description: Identifier of the fluid contact interpretation data record used as an input in deriving the fluid contact TVD.

DissolvedGasRatiosUndersaturatedOilVsDep.title: Dissolved Gas Ratios Undersaturated Oil Versus Depth
DissolvedGasRatiosUndersaturatedOilVsDep.description: A table showing how gas-oil ratio (Rs) OR a bubble point pressure (Pb) changes by depth. Dissolved gas ratios in undersaturated oil for black oil models are calculated from either gas-oil ratio (Rs) versus depth table OR a bubble point pressure (Pb) versus depth table.

Temperatures.title: Temperatures
Temperatures.description: Array of Temperature Values at a given Depth. The usage of Temperature against Depth is mutually exclusive with the usage of any other property

APIGravityValues.title: API Gravity Values
APIGravityValues.description: Array of API Gravity Values at a given Depth. The usage of API Gravity against Depth is mutually exclusive with the usage of any other property.

BubblePointPressures.title: Bubble Point Pressures
BubblePointPressures.description: Array of Bubble Point Pressure Values (Pb) at a given True Vertical Depth (TVD). The usage of Bubble Point Pressure against TVD is mutually exclusive with the usage of any other property.

SolutionGasOilRatios.title: Solution Gas Oil Ratios
SolutionGasOilRatios.description: Array of Gas Oil Ratios in Solution Values (Rs) at a given Depth. The usage of Gas Oil Ratios in Solution against Depth is mutually exclusive with the usage of any other property.

DewPointPressures.title: Dew Point Pressures
DewPointPressures.description: Array of Dew Point Pressure Values (Pd) at a given True Vertical Depth (TVD). The usage of Dew Point Pressure against TVD  is mutually exclusive with the usage of any other property.

VaporizedOilRatios.title: Vaporized Oil Ratios
VaporizedOilRatios.description: Array of Vaporized Oil Ratio Values (Rv) at a given Depth. The usage of Vaporized Oil Ratio against Depth is mutually exclusive with the usage of any other property.

TrueVerticalDepths.title: True Vertical Depths
TrueVerticalDepths.description: Array of True Vertical Depth (TVD) Values to be used as a reference for any other property mapped against depth. This column is required if any other property is populated.

VaporizedOilRatiosUndersaturatedGasVsDep.title: Vaporized Oil Ratios Undersaturated Gas Versus Depth
VaporizedOilRatiosUndersaturatedGasVsDep.description: A table showing how vaporized oil ratio (Rv) or a dew point pressure (Pd) changes by depth. Vaporized oil ratios in undersaturated gas for black oil models with wet gas are calculated from either vaporized oil ratio (Rv) versus depth table OR a dew point pressure (Pd) versus depth table.

Temperatures.title: Temperatures
Temperatures.description: Array of Temperature Values at a given Depth. The usage of Temperature against Depth is mutually exclusive with the usage of any other property

APIGravityValues.description: Array of API Gravity Values at a given Depth. The usage of API Gravity against Depth is mutually exclusive with the usage of any other property.

BubblePointPressures.description: Array of Bubble Point Pressure Values (Pb) at a given True Vertical Depth (TVD). The usage of Bubble Point Pressure against TVD is mutually exclusive with the usage of any other property.

SolutionGasOilRatios.title: Solution Gas Oil Ratios
SolutionGasOilRatios.description: Array of Gas Oil Ratios in Solution Values (Rs) at a given Depth. The usage of Gas Oil Ratios in Solution against Depth is mutually exclusive with the usage of any other property.

DewPointPressures.title: Dew Point Pressures
DewPointPressures.description: Array of Dew Point Pressure Values (Pd) at a given True Vertical Depth (TVD). The usage of Dew Point Pressure against TVD  is mutually exclusive with the usage of any other property.

VaporizedOilRatios.title: Vaporized Oil Ratios
VaporizedOilRatios.description: Array of Vaporized Oil Ratio Values (Rv) at a given Depth. The usage of Vaporized Oil Ratio against Depth is mutually exclusive with the usage of any other property.

TrueVerticalDepths.title: True Vertical Depths
TrueVerticalDepths.description: Array of True Vertical Depth (TVD) Values to be used as a reference for any other property mapped against depth. This column is required if any other property is populated.

EnableFineScaleEquilibration.title: Enable Fine Scale Equilibration
EnableFineScaleEquilibration.description: If false, fluid saturation is calculated at the center of the block. If true, the block is subdivided based on the value defined by FineScaleEquilibration.InitialFluidsInPlaceCalculationAccuracy.

FineScaleEquilibration.title: Fine-Scale Equilibration
FineScaleEquilibration.description: Cohesive set of attributes describing the details of the fine scale equilibration. Expectation is to fill out this attribute if the EnableFineScaleEquilibration is set to true.

InitialFluidsInPlaceCalculationAccuracy.title: Initial Fluids In-Place Calculation Accuracy
InitialFluidsInPlaceCalculationAccuracy.description: This is a number that controls the vertical resolution by subdividing the cell, often used as an input to an equation used by the simulator.

EnableTiltedBlockEquilibration.title: Enable Tilted-Block Equilibration
EnableTiltedBlockEquilibration.description: This indicates whether or not the subdivision should be made parallel to the tilted cell structure in place (true) or purely horizontally (false).

IsQuiescenceActive.title: Is Quiescence Active
IsQuiescenceActive.description: If true, the quiescence option computes a modification to the pressure field such that the reservoir is in hydrostatic equilibrium with respect to the saturations. The pressure modifications are then applied during the rest of the simulation.

RefinementRange.title: Refinement Range
RefinementRange.description: Defines the interval distance both above and below the fluid contacts within which the fine scale equilibrium calculation will be performed.

RefinementDepthStep.title: Refinement Depth Step
RefinementDepthStep.description: Defines the maximum subdivision used in the fine scale equilibrium calculation.

ReservoirSimulationInitialisationDataTyp.title: Reservoir Simulation Initialization Data Type ID
ReservoirSimulationInitialisationDataTyp.description: Indicates whether (i) gas-oil contact and composition data, or (ii) Pressure at datum and composition data is the most relevant data to be honored during the initialization process, or whether simulator should analyze the model to determine this.

FluidModelID.title: Fluid Model ID
FluidModelID.description: Identifies the Fluid Model used for the equilibration

EquilibriumModelSaturationTypeID.title: Equilibrium Model Saturation Type ID
EquilibriumModelSaturationTypeID.description: Identifies the type of saturation system the model was built for, such as a bubble point or a dew point fluid system.

APIGravityVsDepth.description: A table showing how API Gravity changes by depth.

CompositionsAtDepth.description: Array defining the equilibrated compositions at given depths; Also known as a compositional model table

items.title: Composition
items.description: Description of the composition of a mixed fluid at a single depth

CompositionTypeID.title: Composition Type ID
CompositionTypeID.description: Indicating that the table consists of phase component mole fractions versus depth. (Total, Liquid, Vapor, Aqueous, Residual Oil, Solid)

Depth.title: Depth
Depth.description: A depth (TVD) value at which the component mole fractions will be specified

ComponentMoleFractions.title: Component Mole Fractions
ComponentMoleFractions.description: A list of component mole fractions at the designated depth corresponding to the appropriate component id (e.g. 0.0121, 0.0194, etc.). These values should sum up to one.

ComponentNames.title: Component Names

ReservoirSimulationInitialisationTypeID.description: Identifies the initialisation method used for this reservoir simulation, whether enumeration, equilibrium, or mixed.

ReservoirSimulationPropertySets.description: Identifies the grid properties within the associated 3D geologic model that are inputs to the reservoir simulation.

RockModelAssignments.description: Identifies the rock model components (e.g. rock physics model, saturation functions) used as inputs to reservoir simulation and mapped to 3D model regions.

items.description: Describes the association between one rock model component (e.g. rock physics model, saturation functions) and its corresponding allocated region(s) in the 3D static model.

MappingTypeID.title: Mapping Type ID

FluidModelAssignments.title: Fluid Model Assignments

items.title: Fluid Model Assignment

ModelID.title: Model ID

/data/Generated/work-product-component/R.title: ReservoirSimulationRockPhysicsModel
/data/Generated/work-product-component/R.description: A reservoir simulation rock physics model describes the rock compressibility (AKA compaction) of rock, its thermal properties and additional rock physics properties needed for reservoir simulation. It is an input for the task of reservoir simulation (AKA dynamic reservoir modeling). In OSDU, a reservoir simulation rock physics model and a saturation function set are associated to the ReservoirSimulationModel and assigned to the regions defining the rock properties. This rock physics model data object is only intended to support reservoir simulation, not to capture other rock physics data such as acoustic and elastic properties.

MIME Type: image/jpeg
Image Width: 1231
Image Height: 927
Encoding Process: Baseline DCT, Huffman coding
Bits Per Sample: 8
Color Components: 3
X Resolution: 1
Y Resolution: 1
Software: Google
YCbCr Sub Sampling: YCbCr4:2:0 (2 2)

SampleIDs.title: Sample IDs
SampleIDs.description: The samples that the image relates to. One or many Sample relationships are permitted. The Sample object captures attributes of a sample/ specimen (rock or fluid) acquired either through an original acquisition event, sub-sampling event, generated from recombination of other samples / specimens or derived through the application of some laboratory process on the parent sample.

WellboreID.title: Wellbore ID
WellboreID.description: The associated wellbore. This is an optional relationship if the SampleID is populated with the WellboreID.

ImageTypeID.title: Image Type ID
ImageTypeID.description: The type of image. Examples include Photograph, Computed Tomography, Thin Section, etc.

TopDepthMeasuredDepth.title: Top Depth Measured Depth
TopDepthMeasuredDepth.description:
If the top depth is the same as the SampleID record top depth this is an optional property. 
The measured top depth in a wellbore relevant to the image. For a singular point depth the top and base depth should be the same.

BaseDepthMeasuredDepth.title: Base Depth Measured Depth
BaseDepthMeasuredDepth.description:
If the base depth is the same as the SampleID record base depth this is an optional property. 
The measured base depth in a wellbore relevant to the image. For a singular point depth the top and base depth should be the same

VerticalMeasurement.title: Vertical Measurement
VerticalMeasurement.description: The data structure defining the zero depth point for the measured depths as well as the VerticalMeasurementSource (driller's depth or logger's depth), so that it becomes clear whether or not a depth correction is required and if so, in which direction the correction has to be performed (driller's depth to logger's depth or vice versa).

DepthShiftID.title: Depth Shift ID
DepthShiftID.description: The WellLog representation carrying the preferred sample-depth to logging-depth correction or mapping

AcquisitionDate.title: Acquisition Date
AcquisitionDate.description: The date the image was originally taken or acquired

ServiceCompanyID.title: Service CompanyID
ServiceCompanyID.description: The organisation or contractor that originally took or acquired the image

ReferenceIdentifier.title: Image Reference Identifier
ReferenceIdentifier.description: Unique or Distinctive Image Reference Number, Job Number, File Number, Identifier, Label, Name, etc. Typically given by the original image acquisition supplier and as indicated in the report or file. Use this attribute to allow correlation back to the original source document, file, etc.

Remark.title: Remark
Remark.description: Remarks regarding the image acquisition and or processing environment or parameters
Remark.example: Natural light. Taken in the field.

FormatInterval.title: Format Interval
FormatInterval.description: The interval included in the image. Typically used for conventional core. For example 1m or 4m

TextualHeader.title: Textual Header
TextualHeader.description: A free text array to capture the image file header or image parameters for knowledge capture, index and search purposes. Header values can be extracted from, e.g., Exchangeable Image File Format (EXIF) properties, Digital Imaging and Communications in Medicine (DICOM) header properties (such as x-ray intensity) and etc.
example:
File Size: 322 kB
File Type: JPEG
MIME Type: image/jpeg
Image Width: 1231
Image Height: 927
Encoding Process: Baseline DCT, Huffman coding
Bits Per Sample: 8
Color Components: 3
X Resolution: 1
Y Resolution: 1
Software: Google
YCbCr Sub Sampling: YCbCr4:2:0 (2 2)

LightingConditionID.title: Lighting Condition ID
LightingConditionID.description: The type of lighting conditions used when capturing the image. Examples include Ultraviolet, White, Natural, etc

/data/Generated/work-product-component/S.title: SaturationFunctionSet
/data/Generated/work-product-component/S.description: A saturation function set is used to describe the relationship between fluid saturations and other properties such as relative permeability and capillary pressure in porous media, which are key factors in determining fluid flow in reservoir rocks. It is an input for the task of reservoir simulation (AKA dynamic reservoir modeling). In OSDU, a reservoir simulation rock physics model and a saturation function set are associated to the ReservoirSimulationModel and assigned to the regions defining the rock properties.

SeismicFieldTraceDataID.description: Seismic dataset(s) containing unprocessed data, as acquired.

HeaderDescriptionIDs.title: Header Description IDs
HeaderDescriptionIDs.description: Description of the SEG-D headers.   May include a recorded example. The array consists of record IDs, which identify a OSDU file or dataset resource.

ObserverLogIDs.title: ObserverLogIDs
ObserverLogIDs.description: Documents produced during acquisition, containing reports on acquisition activities and progress. The array consists of record IDs, which identify a OSDU file or dataset resource.

LineLogIDs.title: Line Log IDs
LineLogIDs.description: Documents produced at end of each line, including information on shotpoint ranges, tapes, and files. The array consists of record IDs, which identify a OSDU file or dataset resource.

ReceiverLogIDs.title: Receiver Log IDs
ReceiverLogIDs.description: Documents produced during acquisition, including parameters , along with recording QC for each shot. The array consists of record IDs, which identify a OSDU file or dataset resource.

ReceiverInformationTableIDs.title: Receiver Information Table IDs
ReceiverInformationTableIDs.description: Document collected during acquisition which includes a format description and attribute properties.  Typically rows are collected for each line and shotpoint, with information on receivers. The array consists of record IDs, which identify a OSDU file or dataset resource.

ReceiverSignatureIDs.title: Receiver Signature IDs
ReceiverSignatureIDs.description: Receiver response collected during acquisition.  May include response to differing receiver group orientations. The array consists of record IDs, which identify a OSDU file or dataset resource.

SeismicNavigationIDs.title: Seismic Navigation IDs
SeismicNavigationIDs.description: Unprocessed navigation collected during seismic acquisition in formats including P1/11 or P1/90. The array consists of record IDs, which identify a OSDU file or dataset resource.

SourceSignatureIDs.title: Source Signature IDs
SourceSignatureIDs.description: Seismic source recording acquired near the source. The array consists of record IDs, which identify a OSDU file or dataset resource.

SourceInformationTableIDs.title: Source Information Table IDs
SourceInformationTableIDs.description: Document collected during acquisition which includes a format description and attribute properties.  Typically rows are collected for each line and shotpoint, with information on sources, like volume, depth, and timing errors. The array consists of record IDs, which identify a OSDU file or dataset resource.

RecorderResponseIDs.title: Recorder Response IDs
RecorderResponseIDs.description: Recording system  parameters and signature. The array consists of record IDs, which identify a OSDU file or dataset resource.

SeismicAcquisitionReport.title: Seismic Acquisition Report
SeismicAcquisitionReport.description: Reference to a dataset containing the seismic acquisition report.

Seismic3DInterpretationSetID.description: For picks on 3D datasets, reference to the 3D interpretation set (not the application project nor an acquisition survey) that supported this interpretation. Only one of Seismic2DInterpretationSetID or Seismic3DInterpretationSetID may be used, but not both.

Seismic2DInterpretationSetID.description: For picks on 2D datasets, reference to the 2D interpretation set (not the application project nor an acquisition survey) that supported this interpretation.  The seismic geometries (seismic line geometries) needed to interpret the location references are inferred through the interpretation survey.  The WPC SpatialArea may reflect the lines that have the horizon picked on it for shallow search purposes.  Only one of Seismic2DInterpretationSetID or Seismic3DInterpretationSetID may be used, but not both.

InterpretationID.title: InterpretationID
InterpretationID.description: The relationship to the Fault Interpretation that this representation is associated with. The Fault Interpretation record, in turn, contains the relationship to the related interpreted Feature. This named property is intended to constrain the AbstractRepresentation target property to a FaultInterpretation for simplicity and clarity.

RepresentationRole.title: Representation Role
RepresentationRole.description: The RepresentationRole assigned to this SeismicFault. Examples: FaultSticks, Pick, FaultCenterLine.

RepresentationType.title: Representation Type
RepresentationType.description: The Fault RepresentationType assigned to this SeismicFault. Examples: PolylineSet, TriangulatedSurface.

SeismicTraceDataIDs.title: Seismic Trace Data IDs
SeismicTraceDataIDs.description: The seismic volumes/sections on which the fault was picked.

BinGridID.title: Bin Grid ID
BinGridID.description:
The Bin Grid of the fault when coordinates are specified in seismic bin inline/crossline.
When populated this bin grid geometry override the geometry defined by the parent Seismic3DInterpretationSet. If empty and Seismic3DInterpretationSetID is populated, the Seismic3DInterpretationSet.SeismicBinGridID applies.

SeismicLineGeometryIDs.title: Seismic Line Geometry IDs
SeismicLineGeometryIDs.description: The list of explicit 2D seismic line geometries overriding any definitions inferred from Seismic2DInterpretationSet. If empty and Seismic2DInterpretationSetID is populated, Seismic2DInterpretationSet.SeismicLineGeometries[].SeismicLineGeometryID apply.

Seismic3DInterpretationSetID.description: For picks on 3D datasets, reference to the 3D interpretation set (not the application project nor an acquisition survey) that supported this interpretation.  The seismic geometry (bin grid) needed to interpret the location references is inferred through the interpretation survey and no longer explicitly through this object.  The WPC SpatialArea may reflect the survey area that has the horizon picked on it for shallow search purposes.  Only one of Seismic2DInterpretationSetID or Seismic3DInterpretationSetID may be used, but not both.

Seismic2DInterpretationSetID.description: For picks on 2D datasets, reference to the 2D interpretation set (not the application project nor an acquisition survey) that supported this interpretation.  The seismic geometries (seismic line geometries) needed to interpret the location references are inferred through the interpretation survey.  The WPC SpatialArea may reflect the lines that have the horizon picked on it for shallow search purposes.  Only one of Seismic2DInterpretationSetID or Seismic3DInterpretationSetID may be used, but not both.

SeismicPickingTypeID.title: Seismic Picking Type ID
SeismicPickingTypeID.description: The picking method used for the seismic fault.

DomainTypeID.title: DomainTypeID
DomainTypeID.description:
Describes the domain of the interpretation, for example, Depth, Time and Mixed domain types.
The property is added here to be human friendly and support search use cases. 
This information is also captured in the `Fault Interpretation` WPC. Please be mindful to keep both properties synchronised.

Interpreter.title: Interpreter
Interpreter.description: The person or team who interpreted the fault.

SubjectiveClassificationRatingIDs.title: Subjective Classification RatingIDs
SubjectiveClassificationRatingIDs.description: An array capturing the classification of Confidence, Quality & Strength applicable to this interpretation. This is different to data quality.

Remarks.title: Remarks
Remarks.description: An array of remarks, typically from the interpreter, providing a comment or general explanation of the fault.

meta.title: Frame of Reference Meta Data

LiveTraceOutline.description: Polygon showing the coverage of live traces in the trace dataset

BinGridID.description: Reference to the WPC which describes the node positions of the processed bin centers.  These are indexed from the trace file using inline and crossline.

HorizontalCRSID.description: Coordinate reference system of positions in trace header, which matches what is described in BinGrid but is repeated here for convenience and in case bin grid is not defined.  In case of conflict with Bin Grid, this value applies to the coordinates as written into CMPX, CMPY headers. Nevertheless, Bin Grid should be used for mapping purposes.

SeismicLineGeometryID.description: Reference to Seismic Line Geometry for 2D seismic processing which describes the node positions of the processed bin centers.  These are indexed from the trace file using CMP (not trace number).

TraceRelationFileID.description: The SRN of a file within the WPC that shows the relationship between trace index and CMP number if the trace data file CMP header is unreliable (for 2D).

PrincipalAcquisitionProjectID.description: For most datasets, the acquisition project that generated the underlying field data.  For merges, probably absent (see processing project for set of acquisition projects used in processing this dataset).

ProcessingProjectID.description: The processing project from which this trace dataset was produced.  Absent for field data.

Preferred3DInterpretationSetID.description: For a 3D volume (including linear subsets), the id of the Seismic3DInterpretationSet which can be considered the master for the area and of which this trace dataset is a privileged member.  It defines the set of trace datasets of a particular bin grid that form the best set for interpretation (not an acquisition survey).

Preferred2DInterpretationSetID.description: For a 2D line section, SRN of the Seismic2DInterpretationSet which can be considered the master for the area and of which this trace dataset is a privileged member.  It defines the set of trace datasets of a particular cohesive set of 2D processing geometries in a survey area that form the best set for interpretation (not an acquisition survey).

SeismicTraceDataDimensionalityTypeID.description: The dimensionality of trace data sets (not as acquired but as in the dataset), such as 2D, 3D, 4D.

SeismicDomainTypeID.description: ID of the nature of the vertical axis in the trace data set, usually Depth or Time.

Seismic2DName.description: 2D line name or survey name for the 2D group

SeismicMigrationTypeID.description: ID of the Seismic Migration Data Type

SeismicStackingTypeID.description: ID of the Seismic Stacking Type

SeismicAttributeTypeID.description: ID of the Seismic Trace Data Type

SeismicFilteringTypeID.description: ID of the Seismic Filtering Type

Phase.description: Amount of phase rotation applied to data

Polarity.description: Reflection polarity of embedded wavelet.  Normal, Reverse, Plus 90, Minus 90 according to SEG standard.

SeismicProcessingStageTypeID.description: It specifies if the seismic is as acquired, or has been manipulated by a process or workflow before arriving at its current state.

SampleCount.description: Number of samples in the vertical direction.

Difference.description: Indicates if the volume is a product of the difference between 4D surveys

StartTime.description: The sample axis value in the vertical dimension at which Time formatted data starts. Use SeismicDomainType to know which of time or depth pairs is the actual range vs. what is estimated.

EndTime.description: The sample axis value in the vertical dimension at which Time formatted data starts. Use SeismicDomainType to know which of time or depth pairs is the actual range vs. what is estimated.

StartDepth.description: The sample axis value in the vertical dimension at which Depth formatted data starts. Use SeismicDomainType to know which of time or depth pairs is the actual range vs. what is estimated.

EndDepth.description: The sample axis value in the vertical dimension at which Depth formatted data ends. Use SeismicDomainType to know which of time or depth pairs is the actual range vs. what is estimated.

TraceCount.description: How many traces are in the volume

TraceLength.description: Maximum trace length calculated using depth or time start and end points as appropriate according to SeismicDomainType.

TraceDomainUOM.description: UOM for vertical trace domain values

FirstShotPoint.description: The shotpoint that came before all others

LastShotPoint.description: The last shotpoint represented by the data

InlineIncrement.description: Sampling interval of inlines in this dataset (difference in labels between neighboring inlines).

CrosslineIncrement.description: Sampling interval of crosslines in this dataset (difference in labels between neighboring crosslines).

VerticalDatumOffset.description: Datum value, the elevation of zero time/depth on the vertical axis in the domain of SeismicDomainType relative to the vertical reference datum used (usually MSL). Positive is upward from zero elevation to seismic datum).

VerticalMeasurementTypeID.description: Identifies a vertical reference datum type. E.g. mean sea level, ground level, mudline.

ReplacementVelocity.description: Value used to produce vertical static shifts in data

ShiftApplied.description: Indicates how much the data has been shifted from the Vertical Datum (seismic reference datum) in the domain and units of SeismicDomainType and in the sense that a positive number causes a sample to move downward in physical space (lower elevation).

Precision.description: Sample data format in terms of sample value precision 8bit Integer, 16bit Floating Point etc.

WordFormat.description: SRN of a reference value for binary data types, such as INT, UINT, FLOAT, IBM_FLOAT, ASCII, EBCDIC.

WordWidth.description: Size of the word in bytes.

ProcessingParameters.description: Processing Parameters to simply capture process history until full provenance model can be implemented.

ProcessingParameterValue.description: The quantity for the processing parameter. May include units, ordering, and other descriptions.

CoveragePercent.description: Actual nominal fold of the trace data set as processed, expressed as the mode in percentage points (60 fold = 6000%).

TextualFileHeader.description: Character metadata from headers inside file, such as the EBCDIC header of SEGY.  This is an array to capture each stanza separately.

RangeAmplitudeMax.description: The actual maximum amplitude value found in the dataset.

RangeAmplitudeMin.description: The actual minimum amplitude value found in the dataset.

StackAngleRangeMax.description: The stacking angle range maximum used during processing of this trace data set.

StackAngleRangeMin.description: The stacking angle range minimum used during processing of this trace data set.

StackAzimuthRangeMax.description: The stacking azimuth range maximum used during processing of this trace data set.

StackAzimuthRangeMin.description: The stacking azimuth range minimum used during processing of this trace data set.

StackOffsetRangeMax.description: The stacking offset range maximum used during processing of this trace data set.

StackOffsetRangeMin.description: The stacking offset range minimum used during processing of this trace data set.

SeismicWaveTypeID.description: The observed wave mode type in this trace data set (P, Sv, etc).

meta.title: Frame of Reference Meta Data

LiveTraceOutline.description: Polygon showing the coverage of live traces in the trace dataset

BinGridID.description: Reference to the WPC which describes the node positions of the processed bin centers.  These are indexed from the trace file using inline and crossline.

HorizontalCRSID.description: Coordinate reference system of positions in trace header, which matches what is described in BinGrid but is repeated here for convenience and in case bin grid is not defined.  In case of conflict with Bin Grid, this value applies to the coordinates as written into CMPX, CMPY headers. Nevertheless, Bin Grid should be used for mapping purposes.

SeismicLineGeometryID.description: Reference to Seismic Line Geometry for 2D seismic processing which describes the node positions of the processed bin centers.  These are indexed from the trace file using CMP (not trace number).

TraceRelationFileID.description: The SRN of a file within the WPC that shows the relationship between trace index and CMP number if the trace data file CMP header is unreliable (for 2D).

PrincipalAcquisitionProjectID.description: For most datasets, the acquisition project that generated the underlying field data.  For merges, probably absent (see processing project for set of acquisition projects used in processing this dataset).

ProcessingProjectID.description: The processing project from which this trace dataset was produced.  Absent for field data.

Preferred3DInterpretationSetID.description: For a 3D volume (including linear subsets), the id of the Seismic3DInterpretationSet which can be considered the master for the area and of which this trace dataset is a privileged member.  It defines the set of trace datasets of a particular bin grid that form the best set for interpretation (not an acquisition survey).

Preferred2DInterpretationSetID.description: For a 2D line section, SRN of the Seismic2DInterpretationSet which can be considered the master for the area and of which this trace dataset is a privileged member.  It defines the set of trace datasets of a particular cohesive set of 2D processing geometries in a survey area that form the best set for interpretation (not an acquisition survey).

SeismicTraceDataDimensionalityTypeID.description: The dimensionality of trace data sets (not as acquired but as in the dataset), such as 2D, 3D, 4D.

SeismicDomainTypeID.description: ID of the nature of the vertical axis in the trace data set, usually Depth or Time.

Seismic2DName.description: 2D line name or survey name for the 2D group

SeismicMigrationTypeID.description: ID of the Seismic Migration Data Type

SeismicStackingTypeID.description: ID of the Seismic Stacking Type

SeismicAttributeTypeID.description: ID of the Seismic Trace Data Type

SeismicFilteringTypeID.description: ID of the Seismic Filtering Type

Phase.description: Amount of phase rotation applied to data

Polarity.description: Reflection polarity of embedded wavelet.  Normal, Reverse, Plus 90, Minus 90 according to SEG standard.

SeismicProcessingStageTypeID.description: It specifies if the seismic is as acquired, or has been manipulated by a process or workflow before arriving at its current state.

SampleCount.description: Number of samples in the vertical direction.

Difference.description: Indicates if the volume is a product of the difference between 4D surveys

StartTime.description: The sample axis value in the vertical dimension at which Time formatted data starts. Use SeismicDomainType to know which of time or depth pairs is the actual range vs. what is estimated.

EndTime.description: The sample axis value in the vertical dimension at which Time formatted data starts. Use SeismicDomainType to know which of time or depth pairs is the actual range vs. what is estimated.

StartDepth.description: The sample axis value in the vertical dimension at which Depth formatted data starts. Use SeismicDomainType to know which of time or depth pairs is the actual range vs. what is estimated.

EndDepth.description: The sample axis value in the vertical dimension at which Depth formatted data ends. Use SeismicDomainType to know which of time or depth pairs is the actual range vs. what is estimated.

TraceCount.description: How many traces are in the volume

TraceLength.description: Maximum trace length calculated using depth or time start and end points as appropriate according to SeismicDomainType.

TraceDomainUOM.description: UOM for vertical trace domain values

FirstShotPoint.description: The shotpoint that came before all others

LastShotPoint.description: The last shotpoint represented by the data

InlineIncrement.description: Sampling interval of inlines in this dataset (difference in labels between neighboring inlines).

CrosslineIncrement.description: Sampling interval of crosslines in this dataset (difference in labels between neighboring crosslines).

VerticalDatumOffset.description: Datum value, the elevation of zero time/depth on the vertical axis in the domain of SeismicDomainType relative to the vertical reference datum used (usually MSL). Positive is upward from zero elevation to seismic datum).

VerticalMeasurementTypeID.description: Identifies a vertical reference datum type. E.g. mean sea level, ground level, mudline.

ReplacementVelocity.description: Value used to produce vertical static shifts in data

ShiftApplied.description: Indicates how much the data has been shifted from the Vertical Datum (seismic reference datum) in the domain and units of SeismicDomainType and in the sense that a positive number causes a sample to move downward in physical space (lower elevation).

Precision.description: Sample data format in terms of sample value precision 8bit Integer, 16bit Floating Point etc.
Precision.title: Precision

WordFormat.description: SRN of a reference value for binary data types, such as INT, UINT, FLOAT, IBM_FLOAT, ASCII, EBCDIC.

WordWidth.description: Size of the word in bytes.

ProcessingParameters.description: Processing Parameters to simply capture process history until full provenance model can be implemented.

items.title: ProcessingParameters
items.description: Processing Parameters to simply capture process history until full provenance model can be implemented.

ProcessingParameterValue.description: The quantity for the processing parameter. May include units, ordering, and other descriptions.

CoveragePercent.description: Actual nominal fold of the trace data set as processed, expressed as the mode in percentage points (60 fold = 6000%).

TextualFileHeader.description: Character metadata from headers inside file, such as the EBCDIC header of SEGY.  This is an array to capture each stanza separately.

RangeAmplitudeMax.description: The actual maximum amplitude value found in the dataset.

RangeAmplitudeMin.description: The actual minimum amplitude value found in the dataset.

StackAngleRangeMax.description: Post-stack: The stacking angle range maximum used during processing of this trace data set.

StackAngleRangeMin.description: Post-stack: The stacking angle range minimum used during processing of this trace data set.

StackAzimuthRangeMax.description: Post-stack: The stacking azimuth range maximum used during processing of this trace data set.

StackAzimuthRangeMin.description: Post-stack: The stacking azimuth range minimum used during processing of this trace data set.

StackOffsetRangeMax.description: Post-stack: The stacking offset range maximum used during processing of this trace data set.

StackOffsetRangeMin.description: Post-stack: The stacking offset range minimum used during processing of this trace data set.

SeismicWaveTypeID.title: Seismic Wave Type ID
SeismicWaveTypeID.description: The observed wave mode type in this trace data set (P, Sv, etc).

StackAngleRanges.title: Stack Angle Ranges
StackAngleRanges.description: Pre-stack: Sets of trace angle ranges contained within this data set.

items.title: AngleRange
items.description: A range container carrying minimum/maximum angle values.

StackAzimuthRanges.title: Stack Azimuth Ranges
StackAzimuthRanges.description: Pre-stack: Sets of trace azimuth ranges contained within this data set.

items.title: AngleRange
items.description: A range container carrying minimum/maximum angle values.

StackOffsetRanges.title: Stack Offset Ranges
StackOffsetRanges.description: Pre-stack: Sets of trace offset ranges contained within this data set.

items.title: LengthRange
items.description: A range container carrying minimum/maximum angle values.

SortOrderID.title: Sort Order ID
SortOrderID.description: Pre-stack: Defines the sorting order of the trace data as stored in the file(s).

GatherTypeID.title: Gather Type ID
GatherTypeID.description: Pre-stack: the type of gathers in this dataset.

TimeLapse.title: Time Lapse
TimeLapse.description: The contents positions the SeismicTraceData record in context of a time series. This is to be used for time lapse or 4D SeismicTraceData. This structure is optional and absent for SeismicTraceData not part of a time series.

TimeSeriesID.title: Time Series ID
TimeSeriesID.description: The relationship to a TimeSeries work-product-component.

TimeIndex.title: Time Index
TimeIndex.description: The index into the TimeSeriesID's data.UTCDateTimeValues[] or data.GeologicTimeValues[] arrays.

LiveTraceOutline.description: Polygon showing the coverage of live traces in the trace dataset

BinGridID.description: Reference to the WPC which describes the node positions of the processed bin centers.  These are indexed from the trace file using inline and crossline.

HorizontalCRSID.description: Coordinate reference system of positions in trace header, which matches what is described in BinGrid but is repeated here for convenience and in case bin grid is not defined.  In case of conflict with Bin Grid, this value applies to the coordinates as written into CMPX, CMPY headers. Nevertheless, Bin Grid should be used for mapping purposes.

SeismicLineGeometryID.description: Reference to Seismic Line Geometry for 2D seismic processing which describes the node positions of the processed bin centers.  These are indexed from the trace file using CMP (not trace number).

TraceRelationFileID.description: The SRN of a file within the WPC that shows the relationship between trace index and CMP number if the trace data file CMP header is unreliable (for 2D).

PrincipalAcquisitionProjectID.description: For most datasets, the acquisition project that generated the underlying field data.  For merges, probably absent (see processing project for set of acquisition projects used in processing this dataset).

ProcessingProjectID.description: The processing project from which this trace dataset was produced.  Absent for field data.

Preferred3DInterpretationSetID.description: For a 3D volume (including linear subsets), the id of the Seismic3DInterpretationSet which can be considered the master for the area and of which this trace dataset is a privileged member.  It defines the set of trace datasets of a particular bin grid that form the best set for interpretation (not an acquisition survey).

Preferred2DInterpretationSetID.description: For a 2D line section, SRN of the Seismic2DInterpretationSet which can be considered the master for the area and of which this trace dataset is a privileged member.  It defines the set of trace datasets of a particular cohesive set of 2D processing geometries in a survey area that form the best set for interpretation (not an acquisition survey).

SeismicTraceDataDimensionalityTypeID.description: The dimensionality of trace data sets (not as acquired but as in the dataset), such as 2D, 3D, 4D.

SeismicDomainTypeID.description: DEPRECATED: Use the "DomainType" property instead. ID of the nature of the vertical axis in the trace data set, usually Depth or Time.

Seismic2DName.description: 2D line name or survey name for the 2D group

SeismicMigrationTypeID.description: ID of the Seismic Migration Data Type

SeismicStackingTypeID.description: ID of the Seismic Stacking Type

SeismicAttributeTypeID.description: ID of the Seismic Trace Data Type

SeismicFilteringTypeID.description: ID of the Seismic Filtering Type

Phase.description: DEPRECATED: Please use SeismicPhaseID for better interoperability. Amount of phase rotation applied to data

Polarity.description: DEPRECATED: Please use SeismicPolarityID for better interoperability.  Reflection polarity of embedded wavelet.  Normal, Reverse, Plus 90, Minus 90 according to SEG standard.

SeismicPhaseID.description: Reference to the reference-data--SeismicPhase value describing the wavelet phase as estimated/processed for this SeismicTraceData instance.

SeismicPolarityID.description: Reference to the reference-data--SeismicPolarity value describing the polarity for this SeismicTraceData instance.

SeismicProcessingStageTypeID.description: It specifies if the seismic is as acquired, or has been manipulated by a process or workflow before arriving at its current state.

SampleCount.description: Number of samples in the vertical direction.

Difference.description: Indicates if the volume is a product of the difference between 4D surveys

StartTime.description: The sample axis value in the vertical dimension at which Time formatted data starts. Use SeismicDomainType to know which of time or depth pairs is the actual range vs. what is estimated.

EndTime.description: The sample axis value in the vertical dimension at which Time formatted data starts. Use SeismicDomainType to know which of time or depth pairs is the actual range vs. what is estimated.

StartDepth.description: The sample axis value in the vertical dimension at which Depth formatted data starts. Use SeismicDomainType to know which of time or depth pairs is the actual range vs. what is estimated.

EndDepth.description: The sample axis value in the vertical dimension at which Depth formatted data ends. Use SeismicDomainType to know which of time or depth pairs is the actual range vs. what is estimated.

TraceCount.description: How many traces are in the volume

TraceLength.description: Maximum trace length calculated using depth or time start and end points as appropriate according to SeismicDomainType.

TraceDomainUOM.description: UOM for vertical trace domain values

FirstShotPoint.description: The shotpoint that came before all others

LastShotPoint.description: The last shotpoint represented by the data

InlineIncrement.description: Sampling interval of inlines in this dataset (difference in labels between neighboring inlines).

CrosslineIncrement.description: Sampling interval of crosslines in this dataset (difference in labels between neighboring crosslines).

VerticalDatumOffset.description: Datum value, the elevation of zero time/depth on the vertical axis in the domain of SeismicDomainType relative to the vertical reference datum used (usually MSL). Positive is upward from zero elevation to seismic datum).

VerticalMeasurementTypeID.description: Identifies a vertical reference datum type. E.g. mean sea level, ground level, mudline.

ReplacementVelocity.description: Value used to produce vertical static shifts in data

ShiftApplied.description: Indicates how much the data has been shifted from the Vertical Datum (seismic reference datum) in the domain and units of SeismicDomainType and in the sense that a positive number causes a sample to move downward in physical space (lower elevation).

PseudoRadialPressure.title: Pseudo Radial Pressure
PseudoRadialPressure.description: The Horner plot is used to determine if pseudo-radial flow developed during pressure decline. If a semi-log straight line is observed and the line can be extrapolated to a reasonable value of reservoir pressure, then radial or pseudo-radial flow may be affecting the decline behavior. This suggests that the fracture is already closed and that data beyond the point of influence need not be considered in the evaluation of closure.

ResidualPermeability.title: Residual Permeability

FluidThermalConductivity.title: Fluid Thermal Conductivity
FluidThermalConductivity.description: In physics, thermal conductivity is the property of a material describing its ability to conduct heat. It appears primarily in Fourier's Law for heat conduction. Thermal conductivity is measured in watts per kelvin-meter. Multiplied by a temperature difference (in kelvins) and an area (in square meters), and divided by a thickness (in meters), the thermal conductivity predicts the rate of energy loss (in watts) through a piece of material.

FluidThermalExpansionCoefficient.title: Fluid Thermal Expansion Coefficient
FluidThermalExpansionCoefficient.description: Dimensional response to temperature change is expressed by its coefficient of thermal expansion. When the temperature of a substance changes, the energy that is stored in the intermolecular bonds between atoms also changes. When the stored energy increases, so does the length of the molecular bonds. As a result, solids typically expand in response to heating and contract on cooling. The degree of expansion divided by the change in temperature is called the material's coefficient of thermal expansion and generally varies with temperature.

Mutually exclusive with inline bin grid definition via the AbstractGenericBinGrid properties. Only one approach should be populated.

SeismicHorizonID.description: The seismic horizon from which this structure map has been computed.

DomainTypeID.title: DomainTypeID
DomainTypeID.description:
Describes the domain of the interpretation, for example, Depth, Time and Mixed domain types.
The property is added here to be human friendly and support search use cases. 
This information is also captured in the `Horizon Interpretation` and abstract Interpretation fragment. Please be mindful to keep both properties synchronised

/data/Generated/work-product-component/T.description: Well Tubular data contains information on the tubular assemblies and their components for the well, wellbore, or wellbore completion (as appropriate). The tubulars can be tubing, casing or liners or other related equipment which is installed into the well. Tubulars can also be equipment which is lowered into the well in the context of drilling, which is then pulled back out.

ParentWellboreID.description: Identifier of the wellbore the Component is standing in.

ParentAssemblyID.description: Optional - Identifier of the parent assembly (in case of side-track, multi-nesting,…) - The Concentric Tubular model is used to identify the Assembly that an Assembly sits inside e.g. Surface Casing set inside Conductor, Tubing set inside Production Casing, a Bumper Spring set inside a Production Tubing Profile Nipple, Liner set inside Casing, etc. This is needed to enable a Digital Well Sketch application to understand relationships between Assemblies and their parent Wellbores.

TubularAssemblyStatus.description: Record that reflects the status of the Assembly - as 'installed', 'pulled', 'planned',... - Applicable to tubing/completions as opposed to drillstrings

StatusTypeID.description: SRN of a reference value status type

Description.description: Used to describe the reason of Activity - such as cut/pull, pulling,

Date.description: Date the status has been established

SuspensionPointMD.description: In case of multi-nesting of assemblies, the 'point' is the Measured Depth of the top of the assembly though with PBRs the Suspension Point may not be the top.

TubularAssemblyNumber.description: Sequence of the TubularAssembly (Typically BHA sequence)

StringClassID.description: Descriptor for Assembly, e.g. Production, Surface, Conductor, Intermediate, Drilling

ActivityTypeID.description: Used to describe if it belongs to a RunActivity or to a PullActivity

ActivityTypeReasonDescription.description: Used to describe the reason of Activity - such as cut/pull, pulling,…

ArtificialLiftTypeID.description: Type of Artificial Lift used (could be "Surface Pump" / "Submersible Pump" / "Gas Lift"….)

LinerTypeID.description: This reference table describes the type of liner used in the borehole. For example, slotted, gravel packed or pre-perforated etc.

MixedStringIndicator.description: A YES or NO flag indicating the assembly is a mixed string. The length of the assembly may be made up of joints with different tensile strengths, or collapse resistance and yield strengths.

ActiveIndicator.description: Indicates if the Assembly is activated or not

TubularDirection.description: Defines whether the sequence of child tubular components runs either top to bottom, or bottom to top.

TubularAssemblyNominalSize.description: Nominal size (diameter) describing the whole assembly, e.g. 9.625", 12.25

TubularAssemblyTotalLength.description: Total Length of the whole assembly.

DriftDiameter.description: The drift diameter is the inside diameter (ID) that the pipe manufacturer guarantees per specifications. Note that the nominal inside diameter is not the same as the drift diameter but is always slightly larger. The drift diameter is used by the well planner to determine what size tools or casing strings can later be run through the casing, whereas the nominal inside diameter is used for fluid volume calculations such as mud circulating times and cement slurry placement calculations.

MinimumInnerDiameter.description: This is the minimum inner diameter of the whole assembly.

SeaFloorPenetrationLength.description: the distance that the assembly has penetrated below the surface of the sea floor.

AssemblyTopMD.description: The measured depth of the top from the whole assembly

AssemblyBaseMD.description: The measured depth of the base from the whole assembly

AssemblyTopReportedTVD.description: Depth of the top of the Assembly measured from the Well-Head

AssemblyBaseReportedTVD.description: Depth of the base of the Assembly measured from the Well-Head

/data/Generated/work-product-component/T.title: TubularUmbilical
/data/Generated/work-product-component/T.description: An umbilical is any control, power or sensor cable or tube run through an outlet on the wellhead down to a particular receptacle on a downhole component (power or hydraulic line) or simply to a specific depth (sensors). Examples include Gas lift injection tube, Subsea valve control line, ESP power cable, iWire for external gauges, external Fiber Optic Sensor cable. Umbilicals are run outside of the casing or completion assembly and are typically attached by clamps. Umbilicals are run in hole same time as the host assembly. Casing Umbilicals may be cemented in place e.g. Fiber Optic.

/data/Generated/work-product-component/T.title: TubularUmbilical
/data/Generated/work-product-component/T.description: An umbilical is any control, power or sensor cable or tube run through an outlet on the wellhead down to a particular receptacle on a downhole component (power or hydraulic line) or simply to a specific depth (sensors). Examples include Gas lift injection tube, Subsea valve control line, ESP power cable, iWire for external gauges, external Fiber Optic Sensor cable. Umbilicals are run outside of the casing or completion assembly and are typically attached by clamps. Umbilicals are run in hole same time as the host assembly. Casing Umbilicals may be cemented in place e.g. Fiber Optic.

Remark.description: Comments about the velocity model reflecting the thinking of the modeler.  Distinguished from Description which is a general explanation of the model.

ObjectiveType.description: The purpose or intended use of the velocity model, such as Stacking|Depth Migration|Time Migration|Time-depth.

VelocityType.description: Name of the Velocity Type describing the statistic represented, such as RMS|Average|Interval|Instantaneous|Stacking|Migration.

VelocityDirectionType.description: Direction associated with the velocity.  Orientation of velocity specification such as vertical, dip and azimuth.

AnisotropyType.description: Type of anisotropy used in the velocity model

DimensionType.description: Is this model defined along a line, on a surface, for a volume, for a time series?

PropertyFieldRepresentationType.description: Is the velocity field represented as a grid or mesh or..

DimensionNodeCounts.description: The number of grid nodes in each direction (i,j,k)

AverageNodeSpacings.description: The average distance between grid nodes or mesh vertices in each direction (i,j,k).  Note that vertical case is equivalent to sample interval.

TotalNodeCount.description: Total number of vertices in the model.

PropertyNameTypes.description: List of properties represented, eg. Vp, Vs, ....  Length ValuesPerNodeOrCell.

ValuesPerNodeOrCell.description: The number of numerical values stored at each node or cell

CellValueTypes.description: The type of numerical value(s) stored in each grid cell, such as Float or Double.

DiscretisationSchemeType.description: Given a discretisation of a property field (e.g. a  mesh), the value of a property may refer to a vertex, the center of a cell, or the region covered by a cell.  When vertical interpolation is constant, this also includes an indication of Z Grid Registration, which whether the sample value pertains to the top, center, of bottom of grid.

DataSourceReferenceKeys.description: Reference to history in source system, for example Jobpro jobset id, dataset id, workflow id

DataSourceSystem.description: System providing data source history, eg. Jobpro, etc.

InterpolationMethodID.description: For discretely sampled models, the mathematical form of interpolation between nodes, such as linear in space, bicubic spline, linear in time, trilinear, horizon-based.

PropertyUOMIDs.description: Units of measure for each property type in Cell Values.  Array of length ValuesPerNodeOrCell.

SeismicDomainTypeID.description: Vertical domain of velocities.  E.g. Time, Depth.

SeismicDomainUOM.description: Unit of measurement for vertical domain

RecordLength.description: Total depth or time covered by velocity model.  In units of SeismicDomainUoM.

HorizontalCRSID.description: The CRS for surface coordinates used in fault locations if not specified in File.

VelocityAnalysisMethodID.description: Type of algorithm used to derive velocities such as Stacking NMO, Tomography, etc.

FloatingDatumIndicator.description: Boolean to show that datum reference is not a constant.  Any description or horizon information must be described in model file(s).

VerticalDatumOffset.description: Datum value, the elevation of zero time/depth on the vertical axis in the domain of seismicdomaintype relative to the vertical reference datum used (usually MSL). Positive is upward from zero elevation to seismic datum).

VerticalMeasurementTypeID.description: Identifies a vertical reference datum type. E.g. mean sea level, ground level, mudline.

ReplacementVelocity.description: Value used to produce vertical static shifts in data

BinGridID.description: the Bin Grid of the Fault System when coordinates are specified in seismic bin inline/crossline.

WellboreID.title: Wellbore ID
WellboreID.description: The relationship to a Wellbore, to which this WellboreIntervalSet is associated with.

VerticalMeasurement.title: Vertical Measurement
VerticalMeasurement.description: References an entry in the Vertical Measurement array for the Wellbore identified by WellboreID, which defines the vertical reference datum for all marker measured depths of the WellboreIntervalSet Intervals array. It is strongly recommended specifying the VerticalMeasurement.WellboreTVDTrajectoryID  when SubSeaVerticalDepth are populated for the intervals.

StratigraphicColumnID.title: Stratigraphic Column ID
StratigraphicColumnID.description: The optional reference to a stratigraphic column (referring to multiple StratigraphicColumnRankInterpretation) providing the stratigraphic framework for the WellboreIntervalSet. It demonstrates the intent to describe complex, potentially overlapping stratigraphic intervals. Only one of the properties StratigraphicColumnID or StratigraphicColumnRankInterpretationID should be populated.

StratigraphicColumnRankInterpretationID.title: Stratigraphic Column Rank Interpretation ID
StratigraphicColumnRankInterpretationID.description: The optional reference to a StratigraphicColumnRankInterpretation. It expresses the intent of a stratigraphic framework with non-overlapping intervals. Only one of the properties StratigraphicColumnID or StratigraphicColumnRankInterpretationID should be populated.

Intervals.title: Intervals
Intervals.description: Array of Intervals, index-aligned with IntervalProperties.

items.title: Interval
items.description: An interval given either by relationships to top/base markers or standalone top/base depths. To avoid confusion about entry and exit depths the naming convention uses Start as the entry point of the well path into the geologic unit and Stop as the exit point. For unfolded geologic units and vertical wellbores Start is Top and Stop is Base.

IntervalID.title: Interval ID
IntervalID.description: The unique identifier of the interval array member in the data.Intervals[] array. Ideally a UUID.

GeologicUnitInterpretationIDs.title: Interpretation Ids
GeologicUnitInterpretationIDs.description: An array of StratigraphicUnitInterpretation, GeobodyInterpretation or RockFluidUnitInterpretation record Ids associated to this interval.

StartMeasuredDepth.title: Start Interval Measured Depth
StartMeasuredDepth.description: The minimal MeasuredDepth of the interval. In the most common case this is the top.  If this value is associated with a marker then this value is a denormalization of data.Markers[].MarkerMeasuredDepth where the data.Markers[].MarkerID equals to StartMarkerID.

StartSubSeaVerticalDepth.title: Start Sub-Sea Vertical Depth
StartSubSeaVerticalDepth.description: True vertical depth sub-sea of the start of the interval. This is the same as true vertical depth referenced to the vertical CRS "MSL depth". If the start of the interval is associated with a marker then this value is a denormalization of data.Markers[].MarkerSubSeaVerticalDepth where the data.Markers[].MarkerID equals to StartMarkerID.

StartIntervalName.title: Start Interval Marker Name
StartIntervalName.description: Name of the interval start (typically the top); when associated with a marker in a WellboreMarkerSet then this name is a denormalization of data.Markers[].MarkerName where the data.Markers[].MarkerID equals to StartMarkerID.

WellboreID.title: Wellbore ID
WellboreID.description: The relationship to a Wellbore, to which this WellboreIntervalSet is associated with.

VerticalMeasurement.title: Vertical Measurement
VerticalMeasurement.description: References an entry in the Vertical Measurement array for the Wellbore identified by WellboreID, which defines the vertical reference datum for all marker measured depths of the WellboreIntervalSet Intervals array. It is strongly recommended specifying the VerticalMeasurement.WellboreTVDTrajectoryID  when SubSeaVerticalDepth are populated for the intervals.

StratigraphicColumnID.title: Stratigraphic Column ID
StratigraphicColumnID.description: The optional reference to a stratigraphic column (referring to multiple StratigraphicColumnRankInterpretation) providing the stratigraphic framework for the WellboreIntervalSet. It demonstrates the intent to describe complex, potentially overlapping stratigraphic intervals. Only one of the properties StratigraphicColumnID or StratigraphicColumnRankInterpretationID should be populated.

StratigraphicColumnRankInterpretationID.title: Stratigraphic Column Rank Interpretation ID
StratigraphicColumnRankInterpretationID.description: The optional reference to a StratigraphicColumnRankInterpretation. It expresses the intent of a stratigraphic framework with non-overlapping intervals. Only one of the properties StratigraphicColumnID or StratigraphicColumnRankInterpretationID should be populated.

Intervals.title: Intervals
Intervals.description: Array of Intervals, index-aligned with IntervalProperties.

items.title: Interval
items.description: An interval given either by relationships to top/base markers or standalone top/base depths. To avoid confusion about entry and exit depths the naming convention uses Start as the entry point of the well path into the geologic unit and Stop as the exit point. For unfolded geologic units and vertical wellbores Start is Top and Stop is Base.

IntervalID.title: Interval ID
IntervalID.description: The unique identifier of the interval array member in the data.Intervals[] array. Ideally a UUID. IntervalID is also used to associate IntervalProperties via the key column data.IntervalProperties.ColumnValues[0].StringColumn[].

GeologicUnitInterpretationIDs.title: Interpretation Ids
GeologicUnitInterpretationIDs.description: An array of StratigraphicUnitInterpretation, GeobodyInterpretation or RockFluidUnitInterpretation record Ids associated to this interval.

StartMeasuredDepth.title: Start Interval Measured Depth
StartMeasuredDepth.description: The minimal MeasuredDepth of the interval. In the most common case this is the top.  If this value is associated with a marker then this value is a denormalization of data.Markers[].MarkerMeasuredDepth where the data.Markers[].MarkerID equals to StartMarkerID.

StartSubSeaVerticalDepth.title: Start Sub-Sea Vertical Depth
StartSubSeaVerticalDepth.description: True vertical depth sub-sea of the start of the interval. This is the same as true vertical depth referenced to the vertical CRS "MSL depth". If the start of the interval is associated with a marker then this value is a denormalization of data.Markers[].MarkerSubSeaVerticalDepth where the data.Markers[].MarkerID equals to StartMarkerID.

StartIntervalName.title: Start Interval Marker Name
StartIntervalName.description: Name of the interval start (typically the top); when associated with a marker in a WellboreMarkerSet then this name is a denormalization of data.Markers[].MarkerName where the data.Markers[].MarkerID equals to StartMarkerID.

StartMarkerSetID.title: Start Interval WellboreMarkerSet ID
StartMarkerSetID.description: Optional reference to the WellboreMarkerSet containing the interval start (typically the top), with MarkerID equals StartMarkerID.

StartMarkerID.title: Start Interval Marker ID
StartMarkerID.description: Individual markers are not globally identifiable. TopMarkerID is the unique id (MarkerID) of the top interval marker (typically the interval base) in the data.Markers[] array where the data.Markers[].MarkerID equals to StartMarkerID.

StartBoundaryInterpretationID.title: Start Interval Boundary Interpretation ID
StartBoundaryInterpretationID.description: The optional relationship to a HorizonInterpretation, GeobodyBoundaryInterpretation or FaultInterpretation. If the interval start (typically the top) is associated with a marker, this is considered a denormalization of the data.Markers[].InterpretationID for the data.Markers[].MarkerID equals to StartMarkerID.

StopMeasuredDepth.title: Stop Interval Measured Depth
StopMeasuredDepth.description: The maximum MeasuredDepth of the interval (typically the base). If the interval stop is associated with a marker then this value is a denormalization of data.Markers[].MarkerMeasuredDepth where the data.Markers[].MarkerID equals to StopMarkerID.

StopSubSeaVerticalDepth.title: Stop Sub-Sea Vertical Depth
StopSubSeaVerticalDepth.description: True vertical depth sub-sea of the interval stop (typically the base). This is the same as true vertical depth referenced to the vertical CRS "MSL depth". If the interval stop is associated with a marker then this value is a denormalization of data.Markers[].MarkerSubSeaVerticalDepth where the data.Markers[].MarkerID equals to StopMarkerID.

StopIntervalName.title: Stop Interval Marker Name
StopIntervalName.description: Name of the interval stop (typically the base); when associated with a marker in a WellboreMarkerSet then this name is a denormalization of data.Markers[].MarkerName where the data.Markers[].MarkerID equals to StopMarkerID.

StopMarkerSetID.title: Stop Interval WellboreMarkerSet ID
StopMarkerSetID.description: Optional reference to the WellboreMarkerSet containing the top with MarkerID equals StopMarkerID.

StopMarkerID.title: Stop Interval Marker ID
StopMarkerID.description: Individual markers are not globally identifiable. StopMarkerID is the unique id (MarkerID) of the interval stop (typically the interval base) in the data.Markers[] array where the data.Markers[].MarkerID equals to StopMarkerID.

StopBoundaryInterpretationID.title: Stop Interval Boundary Interpretation ID
StopBoundaryInterpretationID.description: The optional relationship to a HorizonInterpretation, GeobodyBoundaryInterpretation or FaultInterpretation. If the interval stop (typically the base) is associated with a marker, this is considered a denormalization of the data.Markers[].InterpretationID where the data.Markers[].MarkerID equals to StopMarkerID.

IntervalProperties.title: Interval Property Values
IntervalProperties.description: An embedded ColumnBasedTable with the properties including their values associated to the intervals in data.Intervals[]. The association is done by array index.

TimeSeries.title: Time Series
TimeSeries.description: Allows to link the geometry of the WellboreMarkerSet to a particular index of a time series. This is particularly useful for intervals referring to fluid contacts where the topology and geometry varies against the time.

To convert a Magnetic azimuth to a True North azimuth, the magnetic declination should be added. Starting value if stations have individual values.

/data/Generated/work-product-component/W.title: WellLog
/data/Generated/work-product-component/W.description: A well log is a data type that correlates a particular measurement or multiple measurements in a wellbore against depth and/or time within that wellbore. When plotted visually, well logs are typically long line graphs (called "curves") but may sometimes be discrete points or intervals. This schema object is intended for digital well logs, not raster log files or raster calibration files, but may be used for the latter in the absence of a defined OSDU schema for these use cases.

ReferenceCurveID.description: The data.Curves[].CurveID, which holds the primary index (reference) values.

SamplingStop.title: Sampling Stop

SamplingDomainTypeID.title: Sampling Domain Type ID
SamplingDomainTypeID.description: The sampling domain, e.g. measured depth, true vertical, travel-time, calendar-time.

CompanyID.title: Company ID

CandidateReferenceCurveIDs.description: Secondary index curves, which are alternative candidates to act as ReferenceCurveID. Generally not populated, except in the cases where multiple reference curves are present, e.g. measured depth and time.

ZeroTime.description: Optional time reference for (calender) time logs. The ISO date time string representing zero time. Not to be confused with seismic travel time zero. The latter is defined by SeismicReferenceDatum.

SeismicReferenceElevation.description: Populated only if the WellLog represents time-depth relationships or checkshots. It is expressed via the standard AbstractFacilityVerticalMeasurement. The following properties are expected to be present: VerticalMeasurementPathID (typically elevation), VerticalMeasurementTypeID as SeismicReferenceDatum, VerticalMeasurement holding the offset to either the VerticalCRSID or the chained VerticalReferenceID in the parent Wellbore.

IsRegular.title: Is Regular Flag
IsRegular.description: Boolean property indicating the sampling mode of the ReferenceCurveID. True means all reference curve values are regularly spaced (see SamplingInterval); false means irregular or discrete sample spacing.

LogRemark.title: Log Remark
LogRemark.description: DEPRECATED: Use the `Remarks` property which utilizes the AbstractRemark fragment, capturing more information about a remark or comment. Log remark provides contextual information during the actual log object acquisition. Explains how the measurement in the wellbore is taken on a point in time or depth. Additional information may be included such as bad weather, tool failure, etc. Usually a part of the log header, log remark contains info specific for an acquisition run, specific for a given logging tool (multiple measurements) and/or a specific interval. In essence, log remark represents the external factors and operational environment, directly or indirectly affecting the measurement quality/uncertainty (dynamically over time/depth) - adding both noise and bias to the measurements.

/data/Generated/work-product-component/W.title: WellOpsNonProductiveTime
/data/Generated/work-product-component/W.description: Non Productive Time (NPT) during Well Operations is the time taken to perform all remedial activities that DO NOT continue to progress towards the planned objective(s). NPT will  include all subsequent time taken to reach the same stage in the work programme prior to the NPT event occurring e.g. reach the same depth before stuck pipe event and back-off etc. NPTs caused by an Equipment Failure may be associated to a DowntimeEvent. An NPT start must align to an Operations Report Activity; similarly, an NPT must end at the end of an Operations Report activity.

ReservoirDatumTrueVerticalDepth.title: Reservoir Datum True Vertical Depth
ReservoirDatumTrueVerticalDepth.description: The true vertical depth value for the reservoir pressure datum used in the analysis for calculation of the reservoir pressure. Note that this may vary from the reference depth record in the master-data Reservoir|ReservoirSegment as can change over the lifecycle of the Reservoir.

ReservoirDatumCalculationSubjectiveClass.title: Reservoir Datum Calculation Subjective Classification Rating ID
ReservoirDatumCalculationSubjectiveClass.description: The subjective quality classification of the datum calculation. E.g. Excellent, Good, Poor etc. A Confidence classification could also be used here if there is an issue with the certainty of the interpretation.

AppliedPressureCorrections.title: Applied Pressure Corrections
AppliedPressureCorrections.description: An array of pressure correction(s) applied when interpreting pressure from the gauge depth to the reservoir pressure datum.

items.title: Applied Pressure Correction
items.description: Pressure correction(s) applied when interpreting pressure from the gauge depth to the reservoir pressure datum. Further context can be applied to the Pressure Correction by the use of Facets e.g. what+Gas, what+Oil, qualifier+Total

PressureCorrectionValue.title: Pressure Correction Value
PressureCorrectionValue.description: The pressure correction value applied when interpreting pressure from the gauge depth to the reservoir pressure datum.

FacetIDs.title: Facet Ids
FacetIDs.description:
Unique Ordered Nested Array with: FacetType, FacetRole, both calling specific references

FacetType: Enumerations of the type of additional context about the nature of a property type (it may include conditions, direction, qualifiers, or statistics). 

FacetRole: Additional context about the nature of a property type. The purpose of such attribute is to minimize the need to create specialized property types by mutualizing some well known qualifiers such as "maximum", "minimum" which apply to a lot of different property types.

ReservoirPressureAtDatumDepth.title: Reservoir Pressure At Datum Depth
ReservoirPressureAtDatumDepth.description: The interpreted reservoir pressure at the reservoir datum depth

Remarks.title: Remarks
Remarks.description: Time stamped remarks associated with the reservoir properties calculation activity

InterpretationResultProperties.title: Interpretation Result Property Values
InterpretationResultProperties.description:
An embedded ColumnBasedTable with the properties including their values associated to the results in data.InterpretationResults[]. The association is done by array index.
This usage can be also manage through dataset with file or DDMS contents.
